chapters.title: From Horeb to Kadesh
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 1

These Are the Words

1These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel beyond the Jordan in the wilderness, in the Arabah opposite Suph, between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth and Di-zahab.

2It is eleven days' journey from Horeb by the way of Mount Seir to Kadesh-barnea.

3And it came to pass in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, that Moses spoke to the sons of Israel according to all that the LORD had commanded him for them,

4after he had struck down Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth, at Edrei.

5Beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses undertook to explain this instruction, saying,

Leaving Horeb

6"The LORD our God spoke to us at Horeb, saying, 'You have stayed long enough at this mountain.

7Turn and set out, and go to the hill country of the Amorites and to all their neighbors in the Arabah, in the hill country, in the lowland, in the Negev and on the seacoast, the land of the Canaanites, and Lebanon, as far as the great river, the river Euphrates.

8See, I have set the land before you. Go in and take possession of the land that the LORD swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, to give to them and to their seed after them.'

Judges for the People

9"At that time I said to you, 'I cannot carry you by myself.

10The LORD your God has multiplied you, and today you are as many as the stars of the heavens.

11May the LORD, the God of your fathers, make you a thousand times as many as you are, and bless you as He has promised you!

12How can I bear by myself the weight of you, your burden and your quarrels?

13Choose for yourselves men who are wise, discerning and known among your tribes, and I will make them your heads.'

14You answered me, 'What you have said is good to do.'

15So I took the heads of your tribes, wise men and known, and made them heads over you, commanders of thousands, commanders of hundreds, commanders of fifties and commanders of tens, and officials for your tribes.

16At that time I charged your judges, 'Hear the cases between your brothers, and judge rightly between a man and his brother or the guest who is with him.

17Do not show partiality in judgment. Hear the small and the great alike. Do not be afraid of any man, for the judgment is God's. The case that is too hard for you, bring to me, and I will hear it.'

18At that time I commanded you all the things you should do.

The Scouts at Kadesh

19"We set out from Horeb and went through all that great and terrible wilderness that you saw, by the way of the hill country of the Amorites, as the LORD our God had commanded us, and we came to Kadesh-barnea.

20I said to you, 'You have come to the hill country of the Amorites, which the LORD our God is giving us.

21See, the LORD your God has set the land before you. Go up and take possession, as the LORD, the God of your fathers, has told you. Do not be afraid and do not lose heart.'

22Then all of you came near to me and said, 'Let us send men ahead of us to search out the land for us and bring us back word of the way we should go up and the towns we shall come to.'

23The thing seemed good to me, and I took twelve men from among you, one man for each tribe.

24They turned and went up into the hill country and came to the valley of Eshcol, and scouted it out.

25They took some of the fruit of the land in their hands and brought it down to us, and they brought us back word and said, 'The land that the LORD our God is giving us is good.'

26But you would not go up, and you rebelled against the command of the LORD your God.

27You grumbled in your tents and said, 'Because the LORD hates us He has brought us out of the land of Egypt, to give us into the hand of the Amorites to destroy us.

28Where are we going up to? Our brothers have made our hearts melt, saying, "The people are greater and taller than we are; the cities are great and fortified up to the heavens; and we saw the sons of the Anakim there."'

29I said to you, 'Do not be terrified, and do not be afraid of them.

30The LORD your God, who goes before you, He Himself will fight for you, just as He did for you in Egypt before your eyes,

31and in the wilderness, where you saw how the LORD your God carried you, as a man carries his son, all the way you went until you came to this place.'

32Yet in this you did not trust the LORD your God,

33who went before you on the way to seek out a place for you to camp, in fire by night to show you the way you should go, and in the cloud by day.

The Oath

34"The LORD heard the sound of your words, and He was angry and swore, saying,

35'Not one of these men of this evil generation shall see the good land that I swore to give to your fathers,

36except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He shall see it, and to him and to his sons I will give the land he has walked on, because he has followed the LORD fully.'

37Even with me the LORD was angry on your account, saying, 'You also shall not go in there.

38Joshua son of Nun, who stands before you, he shall go in there. Strengthen him, for he will cause Israel to inherit it.

39Your little ones, who you said would become plunder, and your sons, who today do not know good and evil, they shall go in there. To them I will give it, and they shall possess it.

40But as for you, turn and set out into the wilderness by the way of the Sea of Reeds.'

41Then you answered and said to me, 'We have sinned against the LORD. We will go up and fight, just as the LORD our God commanded us.' Every man of you strapped on his weapons of war and thought it easy to go up into the hill country.

42The LORD said to me, 'Say to them: Do not go up and do not fight, for I am not among you; otherwise you will be struck down before your enemies.'

43So I spoke to you, but you would not listen. You rebelled against the command of the LORD, acted presumptuously and went up into the hill country.

44The Amorites who lived in that hill country came out against you and chased you as bees do, and beat you down in Seir as far as Hormah.

45You came back and wept before the LORD, but the LORD did not listen to your voice or give ear to you.

46So you stayed in Kadesh many days, as many days as you stayed there.

Notes

  • v1 "These are the words" — elleh ha-devarim, the book's opening words and its Hebrew name, Devarim, Words. The Greek name, Deuteronomion, second law, comes from 17:18, where the king is to write mishneh ha-torah ha-zot, a copy of this instruction; mishneh is a second, a double, and the Greek there reads to deuteronomion touto. The book is Moses speaking to Israel: I said to you.

  • v2 "eleven days' journey" — from Horeb to Kadesh by the direct road is eleven days; v3 dates this speech in the fortieth year. The distance between the two numbers is the story of Numbers.

  • v5 "undertook to explain this instruction" — ho'il… be'er, set about to make plain. Be'er is used of writing words very plainly on stones (27:8). Torah here is instruction, the whole teaching Moses is about to give, not yet a name for five books.

  • vv9–18 judges for the people — Moses tells the choosing of the judges in his own words. In Exodus 18 the advice came from his father-in-law Jethro, look among all the people for capable men (Exodus 18:21); here it is Moses who says it to the people, and the burden of Numbers 11:14, I cannot carry all this people by myself, is behind it.

  • v10 "as many as the stars of the heavens" — the promise to Abraham, count the stars… So shall your seed be (Genesis 15:5), spoken as already true: today you are.

  • v17 "the judgment is God's" — ha-mishpat l'Elohim hu. The judge is not to fear a powerful man because the verdict he gives belongs to God.

  • v28 "fortified up to the heavens" — betsurot ba-shamayim, the scouts' words given as the people heard them. In Numbers 13:28 the report was the cities are fortified and very large; by the time it reached the tents, the walls reached the sky.

  • v31 "as a man carries his son" — ka'asher yissa ish et beno, set against v27, where the people say the LORD brought them out because the LORD hates us.

  • v37 "Even with me the LORD was angry on your account" — Numbers 20:12 gives Moses' exclusion as his own failure at the rock, because you did not trust Me. Here Moses says it was on your account, biglalkhem. Both are in the Torah; Deuteronomy gives it from Moses' side.

  • v44 "as bees do" — ka'asher ta'asenah ha-devorim. In Numbers 14:45 the Amalekites and Canaanites struck them and beat them down as far as Hormah; here the attackers are the Amorites and they swarm.

chapters.title: Edom, Moab, Ammon, and Sihon
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 2

Past Esau's Sons

1"Then we turned and set out into the wilderness by the way of the Sea of Reeds, as the LORD had told me, and we went around Mount Seir for many days.

2The LORD said to me,

3'You have gone around this mountain long enough. Turn north.

4Command the people: You are about to pass through the territory of your brothers, the sons of Esau, who live in Seir. They will be afraid of you, so be very careful.

5Do not provoke them, for I will not give you any of their land, not even a footstep, because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as a possession.

6You shall buy food from them with silver, so that you may eat, and you shall also buy water from them with silver, so that you may drink.

7For the LORD your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. He has known your going through this great wilderness. These forty years the LORD your God has been with you; you have lacked nothing.'

8So we passed by our brothers, the sons of Esau who live in Seir, away from the road of the Arabah, from Elath and Ezion-geber, and we turned and went by the way of the wilderness of Moab.

Moab

9"The LORD said to me, 'Do not harass Moab or provoke them to war, for I will not give you any of their land as a possession, because I have given Ar to the sons of Lot as a possession.'

10(The Emim lived there formerly, a people great and many and tall as the Anakim.

11They too are counted as Rephaim, like the Anakim, but the Moabites call them Emim.

12The Horites also lived in Seir formerly, but the sons of Esau dispossessed them and destroyed them from before them and settled in their place, as Israel did to the land of its possession that the LORD gave them.)

13'Now rise up and cross the Brook Zered.' So we crossed the Brook Zered.

14The time it took us to go from Kadesh-barnea until we crossed the Brook Zered was thirty-eight years, until the whole generation of the men of war had perished from the camp, as the LORD had sworn to them.

15Indeed, the hand of the LORD was against them, to wipe them out from the camp, until they were gone.

Ammon

16"When all the men of war had died and were gone from among the people,

17the LORD spoke to me, saying,

18'Today you are to pass through the territory of Moab, through Ar.

19When you come near the sons of Ammon, do not harass them or provoke them, for I will not give you any of the land of the sons of Ammon as a possession, because I have given it to the sons of Lot as a possession.'

20(It too is counted as a land of Rephaim. Rephaim lived there formerly, but the Ammonites call them Zamzummim,

21a people great and many and tall as the Anakim. But the LORD destroyed them from before them, and they dispossessed them and settled in their place,

22as He did for the sons of Esau who live in Seir, when He destroyed the Horites from before them, and they dispossessed them and settled in their place to this day.

23As for the Avvim, who lived in villages as far as Gaza, the Caphtorim, who came out of Caphtor, destroyed them and settled in their place.)

Sihon King of Heshbon

24"'Rise up, set out and cross the Arnon valley. See, I have given into your hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land. Begin to take possession, and provoke him to war.

25This day I will begin to put the dread and fear of you on the peoples under the whole heaven, who will hear the report of you and tremble and be in anguish because of you.'

26So I sent messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon king of Heshbon, with words of peace, saying,

27'Let me pass through your land. I will keep to the road; I will not turn aside to the right or to the left.

28You shall sell me food for silver so that I may eat, and give me water for silver so that I may drink. Only let me pass through on foot,

29as the sons of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Ar did for me, until I cross the Jordan into the land that the LORD our God is giving us.'

30But Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass through his land, for the LORD your God made his spirit hard and his heart stubborn, so that He might give him into your hand, as He has this day.

31The LORD said to me, 'See, I have begun to give Sihon and his land over to you. Begin to take possession, to possess his land.'

32Sihon came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Jahaz.

33The LORD our God gave him over to us, and we struck him down, with his sons and all his people.

34We captured all his towns at that time and devoted every town to destruction, men, women and little ones. We left no survivor.

35Only the livestock we took as plunder for ourselves, with the spoil of the towns we captured.

36From Aroer, which is on the edge of the Arnon valley, and the town in the valley, as far as Gilead, there was not a town too high for us. The LORD our God gave them all over to us.

37Only the land of the sons of Ammon you did not approach, all the bank of the river Jabbok and the towns of the hill country, and wherever the LORD our God had forbidden us."

Notes

  • v1 "we went around Mount Seir for many days" — va-nasov, we circled. The same verb returns in v3: You have gone around this mountain long enough, rav lakhem sov, the words spoken at Horeb in 1:6, rav lakhem shevet, you have stayed long enough.

  • vv4–6 "your brothers, the sons of Esau" — Edom is brothers because Esau was Jacob's brother. In Numbers 20:14–21 the king of Edom refused passage, Edom came out against them with a large army; this chapter tells of buying food and water from the sons of Esau who live in Seir (vv6, 29) and passing by. The two accounts are given side by side without being joined.

  • v5 "not even a footstep" — ad midrakh kaf ragel, up to the treading of the sole of a foot. Esau's land is as much a gift of the LORD as Israel's: I have given Mount Seir to Esau as a possession.

  • v7 "you have lacked nothing" — lo chasarta davar. Forty years in the wilderness are summed up not as punishment but as provision.

  • vv9, 19 "the sons of Lot" — Moab and Ammon, from Lot's two sons: He is the father of Moab… He is the father of the sons of Ammon to this day (Genesis 19:37–38). Edom, Moab and Ammon are all kin, and all three are left their land.

  • vv10–12, 20–23 the old peoples — the speech breaks off (set in parentheses here) to say who held these lands before: the giants of Moab, Emim, and of Ammon, Zamzummim, both counted among the Rephaim. Genesis 14:5 names the Rephaim and the Emim among the peoples the eastern kings struck; the Horites of Seir are the sons of Seir the Horite (Genesis 36:20). Each people took its land from an older people, and the LORD gave it.

  • v14 "thirty-eight years" — from Kadesh-barnea to the Brook Zered. With the time before Kadesh, it completes the forty years of 1:3, and the oath of 1:35 is kept: that generation is gone.

  • v30 "made his spirit hard and his heart stubborn" — hiqshah… et rucho ve-immets et levavo, the words of Pharaoh's story: I Myself will make Pharaoh's heart hard (Exodus 7:3). Numbers 21:23 says only that Sihon would not let Israel pass; Deuteronomy says why.

  • v34 "devoted every town to destruction" — va-nacharem, from cherem, the vow of Numbers 21:2: I will devote their towns to destruction. What is devoted is given over wholly and nothing is kept, except here the livestock and the spoil (v35).

chapters.title: Og of Bashan, and Moses' Plea
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 3

Og King of Bashan

1"Then we turned and went up by the road to Bashan, and Og king of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.

2The LORD said to me, 'Do not be afraid of him, for I have given him into your hand, with all his people and his land. You shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.'

3So the LORD our God gave into our hand Og king of Bashan as well, with all his people, and we struck him down until no survivor was left to him.

4We captured all his towns at that time. There was not a town that we did not take from them: sixty towns, the whole region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

5All these were towns fortified with high walls, gates and bars, besides a great many unwalled villages.

6We devoted them to destruction, as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon, devoting every town to destruction, men, women and little ones.

7But all the livestock and the spoil of the towns we took as plunder for ourselves.

8So at that time we took the land out of the hand of the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, from the Arnon valley to Mount Hermon

9(the Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir),

10all the towns of the plateau, all Gilead and all Bashan, as far as Salecah and Edrei, towns of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

11(For only Og king of Bashan was left of the remnant of the Rephaim. His bed was a bed of iron; is it not in Rabbah of the sons of Ammon? Nine cubits was its length and four cubits its width, by the cubit of a man.)

The Land Divided East of the Jordan

12"This land we took possession of at that time. From Aroer, which is by the Arnon valley, and half the hill country of Gilead with its towns, I gave to the Reubenites and the Gadites.

13The rest of Gilead, and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh — the whole region of Argob, all Bashan; it is called a land of Rephaim.

14Jair son of Manasseh took the whole region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and called them after his own name, Havvoth-jair — Bashan — to this day.

15To Machir I gave Gilead.

16To the Reubenites and the Gadites I gave from Gilead as far as the Arnon valley, with the middle of the valley as a border, and as far as the river Jabbok, the border of the sons of Ammon,

17and the Arabah, with the Jordan as a border, from Chinnereth as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, under the slopes of Pisgah on the east.

18At that time I commanded you, saying, 'The LORD your God has given you this land to possess. All you men of valor shall cross over armed before your brothers, the sons of Israel.

19Only your wives, your little ones and your livestock — I know that you have much livestock — shall stay in the towns I have given you,

20until the LORD gives rest to your brothers as He has to you, and they too possess the land that the LORD your God is giving them beyond the Jordan. Then each of you may return to his possession that I have given you.'

21At that time I commanded Joshua, saying, 'Your eyes have seen all that the LORD your God has done to these two kings. So the LORD will do to all the kingdoms into which you are crossing.

22Do not be afraid of them, for the LORD your God is the one who fights for you.'

Moses' Plea

23"At that time I pleaded with the LORD, saying,

24'Lord GOD, You have begun to show Your servant Your greatness and Your strong hand. For what god is there in heaven or on earth who can do works and mighty deeds like Yours?

25Let me cross over, please, and see the good land beyond the Jordan, that good hill country and Lebanon.'

26But the LORD was furious with me on your account and would not listen to me. The LORD said to me, 'Enough! Speak to Me no more of this matter.

27Go up to the top of Pisgah and lift your eyes to the west and to the north and to the south and to the east, and look with your eyes, for you shall not cross this Jordan.

28But command Joshua, and strengthen him and encourage him, for he shall cross over before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land that you will see.'

29So we stayed in the valley opposite Beth-peor."

  • v9 "the Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir" — one mountain with three names, like the peoples of 2:10–12 and 2:20, each with its own name for the same giants.

  • v11 "His bed was a bed of iron" — eres barzel. Og is the remnant of the Rephaim, the old giant peoples of 2:11, and his bed is given as proof: nine cubits by four, by the cubit of a man, the ordinary forearm. Is it not in Rabbah? speaks to readers who could go and see it.

  • v14 "Havvoth-jair" — the name Numbers 32:41 gives to Jair's tent villages; here it is laid over all of Argob, Bashan, to this day.

  • v17 "the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea" — two names for one lake, the second the name of Genesis 14:3 and Numbers 34:3.

  • v20 "until the LORD gives rest to your brothers" — yaniach, gives rest, from nuach. The eastern tribes may go home only when the others have rest too.

  • v24 "Lord GOD" — Adonai YHWH, the address Abram uses in Genesis 15:2, Lord GOD, what will You give me? Both men open a request to God with it.

chapters.title: You Saw No Form
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 4

Hear the Statutes

1"And now, Israel, listen to the statutes and the rules that I am teaching you to do, so that you may live, and go in and take possession of the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, is giving you.

2You shall not add to the word that I command you, and you shall not take away from it, so that you keep the commandments of the LORD your God that I command you.

3Your eyes have seen what the LORD did at Baal-peor, for the LORD your God destroyed from among you every man who followed the Baal of Peor.

4But you who held fast to the LORD your God are all alive today.

5See, I have taught you statutes and rules, as the LORD my God commanded me, for you to do in the land you are going in to possess.

6Keep them and do them, for that will be your wisdom and your understanding in the eyes of the peoples, who will hear all these statutes and say, 'Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.'

7For what great nation is there that has a god so near to it as the LORD our God is whenever we call on Him?

8What great nation is there that has statutes and rules as righteous as all this instruction that I set before you today?

The Day at Horeb

9"Only take care, and guard yourself closely, so that you do not forget the things your eyes have seen, and so that they do not depart from your heart all the days of your life. Make them known to your sons and your sons' sons —

10the day you stood before the LORD your God at Horeb, when the LORD said to me, 'Gather the people to Me, and I will let them hear My words, so that they may learn to fear Me all the days they live on the earth, and may teach their sons.'

11You came near and stood at the foot of the mountain, and the mountain burned with fire to the heart of the heavens, with darkness, cloud and thick darkness.

12The LORD spoke to you from the middle of the fire. You heard the sound of words, but you saw no form; there was only a voice.

13He declared to you His covenant, which He commanded you to do, the Ten Words, and He wrote them on two tablets of stone.

14The LORD commanded me at that time to teach you statutes and rules, for you to do them in the land you are crossing over to possess.

No Image

15"So take great care for your lives, since you saw no form on the day the LORD spoke to you at Horeb from the middle of the fire,

16so that you do not act corruptly and make for yourselves a carved image in the form of any figure, the likeness of male or female,

17the likeness of any animal that is on the earth, the likeness of any winged bird that flies in the sky,

18the likeness of anything that creeps on the ground, the likeness of any fish that is in the waters under the earth;

19and so that you do not lift your eyes to the heavens and see the sun, the moon and the stars, all the host of heaven, and be drawn away and bow down to them and serve them, things the LORD your God has allotted to all the peoples under the whole heaven.

20But the LORD has taken you and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be a people of His own inheritance, as you are this day.

21The LORD was angry with me because of you, and He swore that I would not cross the Jordan and would not go into the good land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.

22For I am to die in this land. I am not crossing the Jordan; but you are crossing, and you shall possess this good land.

23Take care for yourselves, so that you do not forget the covenant of the LORD your God, which He made with you, and make for yourselves a carved image in the form of anything the LORD your God has forbidden you.

24For the LORD your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.

Scattered and Sought

25"When you have fathered sons and sons' sons, and have grown old in the land, and you act corruptly and make a carved image in the form of anything, and do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD your God, provoking Him to anger,

26I call heaven and earth to witness against you today that you will quickly perish from the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess. You will not live long on it; you will be utterly destroyed.

27The LORD will scatter you among the peoples, and you will be left few in number among the nations where the LORD will drive you.

28There you will serve gods made by human hands, wood and stone, which neither see nor hear nor eat nor smell.

29But from there you will seek the LORD your God, and you will find Him, if you search for Him with all your heart and with all your soul.

30When you are in distress and all these things have come upon you, in the end of days you will return to the LORD your God and listen to His voice.

31For the LORD your God is a merciful God. He will not let you go, and He will not destroy you, and He will not forget the covenant with your fathers that He swore to them.

There Is No Other

32"For ask now about the former days, which were before you, from the day that God created humankind on the earth, and from one end of the heavens to the other: has anything as great as this ever happened, or has anything like it ever been heard of?

33Has any people ever heard the voice of God speaking from the middle of the fire, as you have heard, and lived?

34Or has any god ever tried to go and take for himself a nation from the middle of another nation, by trials, by signs and by wonders, by war, by a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and by great terrors, as all that the LORD your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?

35You were shown it so that you might know that the LORD is God; there is no other besides Him.

36From heaven He let you hear His voice, to discipline you, and on earth He let you see His great fire, and you heard His words from the middle of the fire.

37Because He loved your fathers, He chose their seed after them, and He Himself brought you out of Egypt by His great strength,

38to drive out before you nations greater and mightier than you, to bring you in and give you their land as an inheritance, as it is this day.

39Know therefore today, and lay it to your heart, that the LORD is God in heaven above and on the earth below; there is no other.

40Keep His statutes and His commandments, which I command you today, so that it may go well with you and with your sons after you, and so that you may live long on the ground that the LORD your God is giving you for all time."

Three Towns of Refuge

41Then Moses set apart three towns beyond the Jordan, toward the sunrise,

42for the one who kills his neighbor unintentionally, without having hated him before, to flee there, so that he may flee to one of these towns and live:

43Bezer in the wilderness on the plateau, for the Reubenites; Ramoth in Gilead, for the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan, for the Manassites.

The Instruction

44This is the instruction that Moses set before the sons of Israel.

45These are the testimonies, the statutes and the rules that Moses spoke to the sons of Israel when they came out of Egypt,

46beyond the Jordan, in the valley opposite Beth-peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, whom Moses and the sons of Israel struck down when they came out of Egypt.

47They took possession of his land and the land of Og king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise,

48from Aroer, which is on the edge of the Arnon valley, as far as Mount Sion, that is, Hermon,

49with all the Arabah beyond the Jordan on the east, as far as the Sea of the Arabah, under the slopes of Pisgah.

Notes

  • v2 "You shall not add… and you shall not take away" — lo tosifu… ve-lo tigre'u. Gara, to take away, is the verb of the daughters of Zelophehad and the heads of their clan (Numbers 27:4; 36:3). The instruction is to be handed on whole.

  • v4 "you who held fast to the LORD" — ha-deveqim, from davaq, to cling, the verb of Genesis 2:24, clings to his woman. At Peor Israel yoked itself to Baal (Numbers 25:3); those who clung to the LORD instead are the ones still alive.

  • v12 "you saw no form; there was only a voice" — u-temunah einkhem ro'im zulati qol. The whole argument of vv15–24 rests on this sentence: at Horeb nothing was seen, so nothing may be made. Temunah, form, likeness, is the word of the commandment, any form of what is in the heavens (Exodus 20:4).

  • v13 "the Ten Words" — aseret ha-devarim, the ten words, the Bible's own name for what English calls the Ten Commandments.

  • vv16–18 male or female… animal… bird… creeping thing… fish — the creatures of Genesis 1 in reverse order: God made the fish and birds, then the animals and creeping things, then humankind male and female (Genesis 1:20–27). Here the list starts with male or female and ends with fish. Nothing that God made may be made into an image of Him.

  • v19 "things the LORD your God has allotted to all the peoples" — asher chalaq, which He divided, apportioned to every people under heaven. Israel is not to bow to them; what the other peoples were given them for, the verse does not say. Verse 20 sets Israel apart: But the LORD has taken you.

  • v20 "the iron furnace" — kur ha-barzel, the smelting furnace in which iron is refined. Egypt was the fire Israel was brought out of.

  • v24 "a consuming fire, a jealous God" — esh okhlah hu, El qanna: the consuming fire of Exodus 24:17, the look of the LORD's glory was like a consuming fire on the top of the mountain, and the jealous God of the commandment (Exodus 20:5).

  • v30 "in the end of days" — be-acharit ha-yamim, the phrase of Jacob's blessing, what will befall you in the end of days (Genesis 49:1), and of Balaam's last oracle (Numbers 24:14). Here it looks past exile to a return.

  • v42 "without having hated him before" — mi-temol shilshom, from yesterday and the day before: there was no old grudge. The towns of refuge of Numbers 35 are set apart for the eastern tribes; the three in Canaan come later.

chapters.title: The Ten Words
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 5

The Covenant at Horeb

1Moses called all Israel and said to them, "Hear, Israel, the statutes and the rules that I speak in your hearing today. Learn them and be careful to do them.

2The LORD our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.

3Not with our fathers did the LORD make this covenant, but with us, we who are all here alive today.

4Face to face the LORD spoke with you on the mountain from the middle of the fire,

5while I stood between the LORD and you at that time to declare to you the word of the LORD, for you were afraid because of the fire and did not go up the mountain. He said:

The Ten Words

6'I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slaves.

7You shall have no other gods before My face.

8You shall not make for yourself a carved image, any form of what is in the heavens above, or on the earth below, or in the waters under the earth.

9You shall not bow down to them and you shall not serve them — because I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, calling the guilt of fathers to account on sons, on the third and on the fourth generation of those who hate Me,

10and doing loyal love to thousands, for those who love Me and keep My commandments.

11You shall not lift up the name of the LORD your God for emptiness, because the LORD will not leave unpunished the one who lifts up His name for emptiness.

12Keep the sabbath day, to keep it holy, as the LORD your God commanded you.

13Six days you shall work and do all your labor,

14but the seventh day is a sabbath to the LORD your God. You shall not do any labor — you, or your son, or your daughter, or your male slave, or your female slave, or your ox, or your donkey, or any of your animals, or the guest who is inside your gates — so that your male slave and your female slave may rest as you do.

15Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God brought you out from there with a strong hand and an outstretched arm. That is why the LORD your God commanded you to keep the sabbath day.

16Honor your father and your mother, as the LORD your God commanded you, so that your days may be long, and so that it may go well with you on the ground that the LORD your God is giving you.

17You shall not murder.

18You shall not commit adultery.

19You shall not steal.

20You shall not answer against your neighbor as an empty witness.

21You shall not covet your neighbor's wife. You shall not desire your neighbor's house, his field, or his male slave, or his female slave, his ox, or his donkey, or anything that is your neighbor's.'

Speak to Us Yourself

22"These words the LORD spoke to all your assembly on the mountain from the middle of the fire, the cloud and the thick darkness, with a loud voice, and He added no more. He wrote them on two tablets of stone and gave them to me.

23When you heard the voice from the middle of the darkness, while the mountain was burning with fire, you came near to me, all the heads of your tribes and your elders,

24and said, 'The LORD our God has shown us His glory and His greatness, and we have heard His voice from the middle of the fire. Today we have seen that God may speak with a human being and he may live.

25But now, why should we die? For this great fire will consume us. If we hear the voice of the LORD our God any more, we will die.

26For who of all flesh has heard the voice of the living God speaking from the middle of the fire, as we have, and lived?

27You go near and hear all that the LORD our God says, and you speak to us all that the LORD our God speaks to you, and we will hear and do it.'

28The LORD heard the sound of your words when you spoke to me, and the LORD said to me, 'I have heard the sound of the words of this people, which they have spoken to you. All that they have said is good.

29If only they had such a heart as this always, to fear Me and keep all My commandments, so that it might go well with them and with their sons forever!

30Go, say to them, "Return to your tents."

31But you, stand here by Me, and I will speak to you all the commandment, the statutes and the rules that you shall teach them, so that they may do them in the land I am giving them to possess.'

32So be careful to do as the LORD your God has commanded you. Do not turn aside to the right or to the left.

33Walk in all the way that the LORD your God has commanded you, so that you may live, and it may go well with you, and you may live long in the land you shall possess."

Notes

  • v3 "Not with our fathers… but with us, we who are all here alive today" — most of those who stood at Horeb have died in the wilderness (2:14–16). Moses speaks to their children as if they had been there: the covenant is made with whoever hears it today.

  • v4 "Face to face" — panim be-fanim, and yet v5 says Moses stood between, and 4:12 that they saw no form. The phrase is about the directness of the speaking, not about seeing.

  • v12 "Keep the sabbath day" — shamor, where Exodus 20:8 has zakhor, Remember. Deuteronomy adds as the LORD your God commanded you, pointing back to Sinai; the command is being repeated, not given for the first time.

  • vv14–15 the reason for the sabbath — in Exodus 20:11 the reason is creation: in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth… and He rested on the seventh day. Here it is Egypt: Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, so that your male slave and your female slave may rest as you do. The LORD our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.
Not with our fathers did the LORD make this covenant, but with us, we who are all here alive today.
Face to face the LORD spoke with you on the mountain from the middle of the fire,
while I stood between the LORD and you at that time to declare to you the word of the LORD, for you were afraid because of the fire and did not go up the mountain. He said:

'I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slaves.
You shall have no other gods before My face.
You shall not make for yourself a carved image, any form of what is in the heavens above, or on the earth below, or in the waters under the earth.

and doing loyal love to thousands, for those who love Me and keep My commandments.

You shall not commit adultery.
You shall not steal.

chapters.title: Hear, Israel
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 6

The Commandment

1This is the commandment — the statutes and the rules — that the LORD your God commanded me to teach you, to do in the land that you are crossing over into, to possess it,

2so that you may fear the LORD your God, to keep all His statutes and His commandments that I command you — you, and your son, and your son's son — all the days of your life, and so that your days may be long.

3Hear, Israel, and be careful to do it, so that it may go well with you and so that you may multiply greatly, as the LORD, the God of your fathers, has spoken to you: a land flowing with milk and honey.

Hear, Israel

4Hear, Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one.

5You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength.

6These words that I command you today shall be on your heart.

7Repeat them to your sons, and speak of them when you sit in your house and when you walk on the road, when you lie down and when you rise.

8Bind them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be as frontlets between your eyes.

9Write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.

When You Have Eaten and Are Satisfied

10When the LORD your God brings you into the land that He swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, to give you — great and good cities that you did not build,

11and houses full of every good thing that you did not fill, and hewn cisterns that you did not hew, vineyards and olive trees that you did not plant — and you eat and are satisfied,

12guard yourself so that you do not forget the LORD, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slaves.

13You shall fear the LORD your God, and Him you shall serve, and by His name you shall swear.

14You shall not go after other gods, from the gods of the peoples who are around you —

15for the LORD your God in your midst is a jealous God — or the anger of the LORD your God will burn against you, and He will wipe you off the face of the ground.

16You shall not test the LORD your God, as you tested Him at Massah.

17Keep, keep the commandments of the LORD your God, and His testimonies and His statutes that He has commanded you.

18Do what is right and good in the eyes of the LORD, so that it may go well with you, and you may go in and possess the good land that the LORD swore to your fathers,

19thrusting out all your enemies from before you, as the LORD has spoken.

When Your Son Asks You

20When your son asks you tomorrow, saying, 'What are the testimonies and the statutes and the rules that the LORD our God has commanded you?'

21you shall say to your son, 'We were Pharaoh's slaves in Egypt, and the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand.

22The LORD gave signs and wonders, great and terrible, against Egypt, against Pharaoh and against all his house, before our eyes.

23Us He brought out from there, so that He might bring us in, to give us the land that He swore to our fathers.

24The LORD commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear the LORD our God, for our good all the days, to keep us alive, as it is this day.

25It will be righteousness for us, if we are careful to do all this commandment before the LORD our God, as He commanded us.'

Notes

  • v4 "the LORD our God, the LORD is one" — four words in Hebrew, YHWH eloheinu YHWH echad, with no verb. They can also be read the LORD is our God, the LORD alone. The first reading says what God is; the second says whom Israel serves. Both claim Him for Israel alone.

  • v5 "with all your strength" — me'od, elsewhere an adverb, very, greatly (as in v3, multiply greatly, me'od). Only here and in 2 Kings 23:25 is it a noun: your muchness, all you have. When Jesus quotes this verse in Matthew 22:37 the list is heart… soul… mind.

  • v7 "Repeat them" — shinnantam, from shanan, to sharpen: go over them until they are sharp. The four times of day that follow — sitting, walking, lying down, rising — cover a whole day.

  • v8 "frontlets" — totafot, a rare word, used also of the Passover sign in Exodus 13:16, where this rendering has a band between your eyes. Jewish practice took vv8–9 literally in tefillin and the mezuzah; Matthew 23:5 mentions the phylacteries.

  • vv10–11 "that you did not build… did not fill… did not hew… did not plant" — four times, asher lo. The gift is the danger: eating what others made, Israel may forget who gave it (v12).

  • v13 "You shall fear the LORD your God, and Him you shall serve" — Jesus answers the tempter with this verse in Matthew 4:10, as the Greek has it: worship in place of fear, and Him only.

  • v16 "as you tested Him at Massah" — Exodus 17:7: they tested the LORD, saying, 'Is the LORD among us or not?' Jesus answers the tempter with this verse in Matthew 4:7.

  • v17 "Keep, keep" — shamor tishmerun, the verb doubled for force.

  • v20 "When your son asks you tomorrow" — the same form as Exodus 13:14, when your son asks you tomorrow, 'What is this?' The answer (vv21–25) is not a rule but a story: We were Pharaoh's slaves.

  • v25 "It will be righteousness for us" — tsedaqah. Keeping the commandment is counted as righteousness, as Abraham's trust was in Genesis 15:6.

chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 7

Make No Covenant with Them

1When the LORD your God brings you into the land that you are going into to possess, and clears away many nations from before you — the Hittite and the Girgashite and the Amorite and the Canaanite and the Perizzite and the Hivite and the Jebusite, seven nations greater and mightier than you —

2and the LORD your God gives them over before you and you strike them, you shall devote them to destruction. You shall make no covenant with them and show them no favor.

3You shall not intermarry with them: your daughter you shall not give to his son, and his daughter you shall not take for your son,

4for he will turn your son away from following Me, and they will serve other gods. Then the anger of the LORD will burn against you, and He will wipe you out quickly.

5Rather, this is what you shall do to them: tear down their altars, shatter their standing stones, cut down their sacred poles, and burn their carved images with fire.

Why the LORD Chose You

6For you are a holy people to the LORD your God. The LORD your God has chosen you to be a people for His own treasure, out of all the peoples who are on the face of the ground.

7Not because you were more numerous than all the peoples did the LORD set His heart on you and choose you — for you were the fewest of all the peoples —

8but because the LORD loved you, and because He kept the oath that He swore to your fathers, the LORD brought you out with a strong hand and redeemed you from the house of slaves, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.

9Know, then, that the LORD your God is God, the faithful God, who keeps covenant and loyal love to a thousand generations with those who love Him and keep His commandments,

10and repays to their face those who hate Him, to destroy them. He will not delay with the one who hates Him; to his face He will repay him.

11Keep the commandment and the statutes and the rules that I command you today, to do them.

Blessed Above All Peoples

12And it will come to pass, because you listen to these rules and keep and do them, that the LORD your God will keep for you the covenant and the loyal love that He swore to your fathers.

13He will love you and bless you and multiply you. He will bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground, your grain and your new wine and your oil, the offspring of your cattle and the young of your flock, on the ground that He swore to your fathers to give you.

14You will be blessed above all the peoples. There will be no barren male or barren female among you, or among your animals.

15The LORD will take away from you every sickness, and none of the evil diseases of Egypt that you knew will He put on you; He will lay them on all who hate you.

16You shall consume all the peoples that the LORD your God is giving you. Your eye shall not pity them, and you shall not serve their gods, for that would be a snare to you.

Do Not Be Afraid of Them

17If you say in your heart, 'These nations are greater than I; how can I drive them out?'

18do not be afraid of them. Remember, remember what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and to all Egypt —

19the great trials that your eyes saw, the signs and the wonders, the strong hand and the outstretched arm by which the LORD your God brought you out. So the LORD your God will do to all the peoples you are afraid of.

20The LORD your God will also send the hornet among them, until those who are left and those who hide from you are destroyed.

21Do not tremble before them, for the LORD your God is in your midst, a great and awesome God.

22The LORD your God will clear away these nations from before you little by little. You will not be able to finish them off quickly, or the beasts of the field would multiply against you.

23The LORD your God will give them over before you and throw them into great confusion, until they are destroyed.

24He will give their kings into your hand, and you will wipe out their name from under the heavens. No one will be able to stand before you until you have destroyed them.

25The carved images of their gods you shall burn with fire. You shall not covet the silver or the gold on them and take it for yourself, or you will be snared by it, for it is detestable to the LORD your God.

26You shall not bring a detestable thing into your house, or you will be devoted to destruction like it. You shall utterly loathe it and utterly detest it, for it is devoted to destruction.

Notes

  • v2 "you shall devote them to destruction" — hacharem tacharim, the verb doubled. Cherem removes a thing from human use and gives it wholly to God; nothing of it may be kept (vv25–26).

  • v3 "You shall not intermarry with them" — the reason given is not blood but worship: he will turn your son away from following Me (v4).

  • v6 "for His own treasure" — segullah, the word of Exodus 19:5, you will be My own treasure out of all the peoples: a king's private wealth, set apart from what he governs.

  • vv7–8 "Not because you were more numerous… but because the LORD loved you" — the choice is explained by nothing in Israel. Chashaq, set His heart on, is a word of desire, used of a man drawn to a woman in 21:11. Then the reason given is only love, and the oath to the fathers.

  • v10 "to their face" — el panav, twice: God repays the one who hates Him directly and in person, not by waiting on his children (compare 5:9, on the third and on the fourth generation).

  • v12 "because you listen" — eqev, heel, used as because: the reward that follows on the heel of the listening. The portion of the Torah read in synagogues from here takes its name from the word.

  • v20 "the hornet" — tzir'ah, as in Exodus 23:28: one of three places the word occurs, all this same promise.

  • v22 "little by little… or the beasts of the field would multiply against you" — the promise of Exodus 23:29–30, I will not drive them out from before you in one year.

  • vv25–26 "detestable… loathe… detest" — to'evah, then the verbs shaqqets teshaqqetzennu and ta'ev teta'avennu, each doubled. Whoever takes a thing devoted to destruction becomes cherem with it: after Achan takes from the spoil of Jericho, God says of Israel, they have become devoted to destruction (Joshua 7:12).

chapters.title: Not on Bread Alone
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 8

Remember the Way

1All the commandment that I command you today you shall be careful to do, so that you may live and multiply, and go in and possess the land that the LORD swore to your fathers.

2Remember all the way that the LORD your God has led you these forty years in the wilderness, to humble you, to test you, to know what was in your heart — whether you would keep His commandments or not.

3He humbled you and let you hunger and fed you with manna, which you did not know and your fathers did not know, to make you know that a person does not live on bread alone, but on everything that comes out of the mouth of the LORD.

4Your clothing did not wear out on you, and your foot did not swell, these forty years.

5Know in your heart that as a man disciplines his son, the LORD your God disciplines you.

6Keep the commandments of the LORD your God, to walk in His ways and to fear Him.

A Good Land

7For the LORD your God is bringing you into a good land, a land of streams of water, of springs and deeps coming out in the valley and on the hill,

8a land of wheat and barley, of vine and fig and pomegranate, a land of olive oil and honey,

9a land where you will eat bread without scarcity, where you will lack nothing, a land whose stones are iron and out of whose hills you will dig copper.

10You will eat and be satisfied, and you shall bless the LORD your God for the good land that He has given you.

Do Not Forget

11Guard yourself so that you do not forget the LORD your God by not keeping His commandments and His rules and His statutes that I command you today —

12so that, when you have eaten and are satisfied, and have built good houses and live in them,

13and your herds and your flocks multiply, and silver and gold multiply for you, and all that you have multiplies,

14your heart is not lifted up and you forget the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slaves,

15who led you through the great and terrible wilderness, with its fiery serpents and scorpions, a thirsty ground where there was no water; who brought water out for you from the flint rock;

16who fed you in the wilderness with manna that your fathers did not know, to humble you and to test you, to do you good in the end —

17and you say in your heart, 'My power and the might of my hand have made me this wealth.'

18Remember the LORD your God, for it is He who gives you power to make wealth, so that He may confirm His covenant that He swore to your fathers, as it is this day.

19And it shall come to pass, if you forget, forget the LORD your God and go after other gods and serve them and bow down to them, I testify against you today that you will perish, perish.

20Like the nations that the LORD is destroying before you, so you will perish, because you would not listen to the voice of the LORD your God.

Notes

  • v2 "to humble you, to test you" — 'annotekha, from 'anah, the verb used of Egypt's hard labor in Exodus 1:11. The wilderness pressed on Israel too, but for a purpose: to know what was in your heart.

  • v3 "does not live on bread alone" — the manna was bread no one had known, and the lesson was hunger first, then food. Jesus answers the tempter with this verse in Matthew 4:4, after forty days without food in the wilderness.

  • v4 "Your clothing did not wear out" — the same claim is made again in 29:5, where the sandals are added.

  • v5 "as a man disciplines his son" — yasar, to discipline, to instruct: the wilderness years were a father's training, not a sentence.

  • vv7–8 the land's seven kinds — wheat, barley, vine, fig, pomegranate, olive, and devash, honey, which here stands in a list of plants and so may mean date syrup as well as bees' honey.

  • v9 "whose stones are iron… you will dig copper" — nechoshet is the same word as bronze in the tabernacle; the ore is copper, the alloy is bronze.

  • v15 "fiery serpents" — nachash saraph, the snakes of Numbers 21:6. Saraph is from the verb to burn, perhaps from the burning of the bite.

  • v17 "My power and the might of my hand" — kochi ve-otsem yadi. The danger this chapter names is not hunger in the wilderness but plenty in the land (vv12–14).

  • vv19–20 "you will perish, perish… Like the nations" — avod tovedun, the verb doubled. The nations are being destroyed for the same reason Israel would be; there is no separate rule for the chosen people.

chapters.title: Not for Your Righteousness
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 9

A Consuming Fire Goes Before You

1Hear, Israel: you are crossing the Jordan today to go in and dispossess nations greater and mightier than you, cities great and fortified up to the heavens,

2a people great and tall, the sons of the Anakim, whom you know, and of whom you have heard it said, 'Who can stand before the sons of Anak?'

3Know today that the LORD your God is the one crossing over before you, a consuming fire. He will destroy them and He will bring them down before you, and you will drive them out and make them perish quickly, as the LORD has spoken to you.

Not for Your Righteousness

4Do not say in your heart, when the LORD your God thrusts them out from before you, 'Because of my righteousness the LORD has brought me in to possess this land.' It is because of the wickedness of these nations that the LORD is driving them out from before you.

5Not because of your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart are you going in to possess their land, but because of the wickedness of these nations the LORD your God is driving them out from before you, and to confirm the word that the LORD swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob.

6Know, then, that it is not because of your righteousness that the LORD your God is giving you this good land to possess, for you are a stiff-necked people.

The Calf at Horeb

7Remember — do not forget — how you provoked the LORD your God to anger in the wilderness. From the day you came out of the land of Egypt until you came to this place, you have been rebellious against the LORD.

8At Horeb you provoked the LORD to anger, and the LORD was so angry with you that He was ready to destroy you.

9When I went up the mountain to receive the tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant that the LORD made with you, I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water.

10The LORD gave me the two tablets of stone written by the finger of God, and on them were all the words that the LORD spoke with you on the mountain from the middle of the fire on the day of the assembly.

11It came to pass at the end of forty days and forty nights that the LORD gave me the two tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant.

12The LORD said to me, 'Get up, go down quickly from here, for your people whom you brought out of Egypt have acted corruptly. They have turned aside quickly from the way that I commanded them; they have made themselves a molten image.'

13The LORD said to me, 'I have seen this people, and it is a stiff-necked people.

14Leave Me alone, and I will destroy them and wipe out their name from under the heavens, and I will make you into a nation mightier and more numerous than they.'

15So I turned and went down from the mountain, while the mountain was burning with fire, and the two tablets of the covenant were in my two hands.

16I looked, and you had sinned against the LORD your God. You had made yourselves a molten calf. You had turned aside quickly from the way that the LORD had commanded you.

17I took hold of the two tablets and threw them from my two hands and broke them before your eyes.

Forty Days on My Face

18Then I fell down before the LORD as at the first, forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water, because of all the sin you had committed, doing what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, to provoke Him.

19For I was afraid of the anger and the fury with which the LORD was angry with you, ready to destroy you. The LORD listened to me that time also.

20With Aaron the LORD was very angry, ready to destroy him, and I prayed for Aaron too at that time.

21Your sin, the calf you had made, I took and burned it with fire and crushed it, grinding it thoroughly until it was as fine as dust, and I threw its dust into the stream that comes down from the mountain.

22At Taberah, and at Massah, and at Kibroth-hattaavah you provoked the LORD to anger.

23When the LORD sent you from Kadesh-barnea, saying, 'Go up and possess the land that I have given you,' you rebelled against the command of the LORD your God. You did not trust Him and did not listen to His voice.

24You have been rebellious against the LORD from the day I knew you.

25So I fell down before the LORD the forty days and the forty nights that I fell down, because the LORD had said He would destroy you.

26I prayed to the LORD and said, 'Lord GOD, do not destroy Your people, Your inheritance, whom You redeemed by Your greatness, whom You brought out of Egypt with a strong hand.

27Remember Your servants, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Do not look at the stubbornness of this people, or at its wickedness, or at its sin.

28Otherwise the land You brought us out of will say, "Because the LORD was not able to bring them into the land that He promised them, and because He hated them, He brought them out to kill them in the wilderness."

29They are Your people and Your inheritance, whom You brought out by Your great power and by Your outstretched arm.'

Notes

  • v3 "a consuming fire" — esh okhelah, as in 4:24, the LORD your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God. There the fire is a warning to Israel; here it goes ahead of Israel against the nations.

  • vv4–6 "Not because of your righteousness" — three times. Chapter 7 said the choice was not for Israel's size (7:7); this chapter says the land is not for Israel's goodness. What remains is the wickedness of the nations and the oath to the fathers.

  • v6 "a stiff-necked people" — am qesheh oref, God's own verdict at the calf in Exodus 32:9, which Moses repeats here (v13) before telling the story that proves it.

  • v10 "on the day of the assembly" — yom ha-qahal, the day of 4:10, the day you stood before the LORD your God at Horeb. The Greek here has hēmera ekklēsias: ekklēsia, the word the New Testament uses for the church.

  • v16 "a molten calf" — egel massekhah, the words of Exodus 32:4. In v12 God tells Moses what the people have done; in v16 Moses sees it for himself, in the same words.

  • v18 "as at the first" — Moses tells of a second forty days without food, as in v9. Exodus 34:28 gives forty days for the second tablets; Deuteronomy makes them days of prayer for the people.

  • v21 "Your sin, the calf" — the object itself is called chattatkhem, your sin. Exodus 32:20 has the people drink the water; here the dust goes into the stream that comes down from the mountain, the stream they drank from.

  • v22 Taberah, Massah, Kibroth-hattaavah — the fire of Numbers 11:3, the testing of Exodus 17:7, and the graves of craving of Numbers 11:34. Three more places, before Kadesh (v23), where Israel provoked God.

  • vv26–29 Moses' prayer — he gives God three reasons, and none of them is Israel's goodness: Your people, Your inheritance; Remember Your servants; and what Egypt would say (compare Exodus 32:12).

chapters.title: What the LORD Asks of You
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 10

The Second Tablets

1At that time the LORD said to me, 'Cut for yourself two tablets of stone like the first ones, and come up to Me on the mountain, and make yourself an ark of wood.

2I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke, and you shall put them in the ark.'

3So I made an ark of acacia wood, and cut two tablets of stone like the first ones, and went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hand.

4He wrote on the tablets, as in the first writing, the Ten Words that the LORD had spoken to you on the mountain from the middle of the fire on the day of the assembly, and the LORD gave them to me.

5Then I turned and came down from the mountain and put the tablets in the ark that I had made, and there they are, as the LORD commanded me.

6The sons of Israel set out from Beeroth Bene-jaakan to Moserah. There Aaron died, and there he was buried, and Eleazar his son served as priest in his place.

7From there they set out to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land of streams of water.

8At that time the LORD set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the covenant of the LORD, to stand before the LORD to serve Him, and to bless in His name, to this day.

9That is why Levi has no share or inheritance with his brothers; the LORD is his inheritance, as the LORD your God said to him.

10I stayed on the mountain, as in the first days, forty days and forty nights, and the LORD listened to me that time also. The LORD was not willing to destroy you.

11The LORD said to me, 'Get up, go on your journey before the people, so that they may go in and possess the land that I swore to their fathers to give them.'

What the LORD Asks of You

12And now, Israel, what does the LORD your God ask of you but to fear the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways and to love Him, and to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul,

13to keep the commandments of the LORD and His statutes that I command you today, for your good?

14The heavens and the heavens of the heavens belong to the LORD your God, the earth and all that is in it.

15Yet on your fathers the LORD set His heart, to love them, and He chose their seed after them — you — out of all the peoples, as it is this day.

16Circumcise, then, the foreskin of your heart, and do not stiffen your neck any longer.

17For the LORD your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great God, mighty and awesome, who shows no partiality and takes no bribe.

18He does justice for the orphan and the widow, and loves the guest, giving him bread and clothing.

19Love the guest, then, for you were guests in the land of Egypt.

20You shall fear the LORD your God. Him you shall serve, and to Him you shall hold fast, and by His name you shall swear.

21He is your praise and He is your God, who has done for you these great and awesome things that your eyes have seen.

22With seventy souls your fathers went down to Egypt, and now the LORD your God has made you like the stars of the heavens for multitude.

Notes

  • v1 "make yourself an ark of wood" — in Exodus the ark is commanded in 25:10 and built by Bezalel in 37:1, of acacia wood overlaid with gold. Deuteronomy tells only what the ark is for: a box to keep the tablets in (v5, there they are).

  • v4 "as in the first writing" — ka-mikhtav ha-rishon. The words are the same; the stones are new, cut by Moses (v3), where the first were the work of God (Exodus 32:16).

  • vv6–7 Aaron's death at Moserah — Numbers 33:38 places it at Mount Hor, and Numbers 33:31–33 has the stations in another order: Moseroth… Bene-jaakan… Hor-haggidgad… Jotbathah. Moserah and Moseroth are the same name, singular and plural; Deuteronomy may be naming the district where Mount Hor stood. The two lists are left as each has it.

  • v8 "At that time" — the Levites are set apart after the calf, as in Exodus 32:26–29, where they rally to Moses.

  • v9 "the LORD is his inheritance" — the promise to Aaron in Numbers 18:20, I am your share and your inheritance.

  • v12 "what does the LORD your God ask of you" — mah… sho'el me'immakh. Micah 6:8 asks a like question, with doresh, require, and gives its own answer.

  • v16 "Circumcise… the foreskin of your heart" — orlat levavkhem. Leviticus 26:41 spoke of their uncircumcised heart; here the people are told to do the cutting themselves. In 30:6 God promises to do it: the LORD your God will circumcise your heart.

  • v17 "God of gods and Lord of lords" — the Hebrew way of saying the highest: Elohei ha-elohim va-Adonei ha-adonim. Lo yissa fanim, does not lift faces, is the idiom for partiality.

  • vv18–19 "loves the guest… Love the guest, then" — the command copies God: He loves the ger, so Israel must. Exodus 22:21 and 23:9 gave the same reason: you were guests in the land of Egypt.

  • v22 "With seventy souls" — the count of Genesis 46:27, All the souls of the house of Jacob coming to Egypt: seventy, set against the promise of Genesis 15:5, count the stars.

chapters.title: The Blessing and the Curse
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 11

What Your Eyes Have Seen

1Love the LORD your God, and keep His charge, His statutes and His rules and His commandments, all the days.

2Know today — for I am not speaking to your sons, who have not known and have not seen — the discipline of the LORD your God, His greatness, His strong hand and His outstretched arm,

3His signs and His works that He did in the middle of Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to all his land,

4and what He did to the army of Egypt, to its horses and its chariots: how He made the waters of the Sea of Reeds flow over them as they pursued you, and the LORD destroyed them to this day;

5and what He did for you in the wilderness, until you came to this place;

6and what He did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab son of Reuben, when the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, and their households and their tents and every standing thing that followed them, in the middle of all Israel.

7For your own eyes have seen all the great work of the LORD that He did.

A Land the LORD Cares For

8Keep all the commandment that I command you today, so that you may be strong, and go in and possess the land that you are crossing over into, to possess it,

9and so that you may prolong your days on the ground that the LORD swore to your fathers to give to them and to their seed, a land flowing with milk and honey.

10For the land that you are going into to possess is not like the land of Egypt that you came out of, where you sowed your seed and watered it with your foot, like a vegetable garden.

11The land that you are crossing over into, to possess it, is a land of hills and valleys; it drinks water by the rain of the heavens,

12a land that the LORD your God cares for. The eyes of the LORD your God are always on it, from the beginning of the year to the end of the year.

Rain in Its Season

13And it shall come to pass, if you listen, listen to My commandments that I command you today, to love the LORD your God and to serve Him with all your heart and with all your soul,

14I will give the rain of your land in its season, the early rain and the late rain, and you will gather in your grain and your new wine and your oil.

15I will give grass in your field for your animals, and you will eat and be satisfied.

16Guard yourselves so that your heart is not enticed, and you turn aside and serve other gods and bow down to them.

17Then the anger of the LORD will burn against you, and He will shut up the heavens so that there is no rain, and the ground will not give its produce, and you will perish quickly from the good land that the LORD is giving you.

Lay Up These Words

18Put these words of Mine on your heart and on your soul. Bind them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be as frontlets between your eyes.

19Teach them to your sons, speaking of them when you sit in your house and when you walk on the road, when you lie down and when you rise.

20Write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates,

21so that your days and the days of your sons may be many on the ground that the LORD swore to your fathers to give them, as long as the heavens are above the earth.

22For if you are careful to keep all this commandment that I command you, to do it — to love the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways and to hold fast to Him —

23the LORD will drive out all these nations from before you, and you will dispossess nations greater and mightier than you.

24Every place on which the sole of your foot treads will be yours. From the wilderness and Lebanon, from the river, the river Euphrates, to the western sea will be your border.

25No one will be able to stand before you. The LORD your God will lay the dread of you and the fear of you on all the land that you tread on, as He has spoken to you.

Gerizim and Ebal

26See, I am setting before you today a blessing and a curse:

27the blessing, if you listen to the commandments of the LORD your God that I command you today;

28and the curse, if you do not listen to the commandments of the LORD your God, but turn aside from the way that I command you today, to go after other gods that you have not known.

29And it shall come to pass, when the LORD your God brings you into the land that you are going into to possess, you shall set the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.

30Are they not beyond the Jordan, past the road toward the setting of the sun, in the land of the Canaanite who lives in the Arabah, opposite Gilgal, beside the oaks of Moreh?

31For you are crossing the Jordan to go in and possess the land that the LORD your God is giving you. You will possess it and live in it,

32and you shall be careful to do all the statutes and the rules that I am setting before you today.

Notes

  • v2 "for I am not speaking to your sons" — the sentence in Hebrew breaks off and restarts, as speech does. Moses insists on eyewitnesses: your own eyes have seen (v7).

  • v6 "every standing thing that followed them" — kol ha-yequm asher be-ragleihem, every standing thing at their feet. Yequm is the rare word of the flood, every standing thing that I have made (Genesis 7:4), and occurs only in the flood story (Genesis 7:4, 7:23) and here. Korah is not named, only the Reubenites of Numbers 16.

  • v10 "watered it with your foot" — hishqita ve-raglekha. Egypt's fields drank from the Nile by channels opened and closed with the foot, or water wheels worked by foot. The land ahead depends on rain, which no one can command.

  • v12 "a land that the LORD your God cares for" — doresh otah, seeks it out. The dependence on rain (v11) is also a closeness: God's eyes are on this land all year.

  • v14 "the early rain and the late rain" — yoreh u-malqosh: the autumn rains that soften the ground for plowing, and the spring rains that fill the grain before harvest.

  • vv13–21 — the second passage of the Shema in Jewish prayer, after 6:4–9, and written with it in the tefillin and the mezuzah. Verses 18–20 repeat 6:6–9, now spoken to you in the plural.

  • v24 "Every place on which the sole of your foot treads" — repeated to Joshua in Joshua 1:3.

  • vv29–30 Gerizim and Ebal — two mountains facing each other above Shechem, beside the oaks of Moreh, where Abram first stopped in the land (Genesis 12:6) and God first promised it to his seed. The ceremony is laid out in chapter 27 and done in Joshua 8:30–35.

chapters.title: The Place the LORD Will Choose
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 12

Not in Every Place

1These are the statutes and the rules that you shall be careful to do in the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, has given you to possess, all the days that you live on the ground.

2You shall utterly destroy all the places where the nations you are dispossessing served their gods, on the high mountains and on the hills and under every leafy tree.

3Tear down their altars, shatter their standing stones, burn their sacred poles with fire, and cut down the carved images of their gods, and destroy their name from that place.

4You shall not do so to the LORD your God.

5Rather, you shall seek the place that the LORD your God will choose out of all your tribes to put His name there, for His dwelling, and there you shall go.

6There you shall bring your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and the contribution of your hand, your vows and your freewill offerings, and the firstborn of your herd and of your flock.

7There you shall eat before the LORD your God, and you shall rejoice in all that you put your hand to, you and your households, because the LORD your God has blessed you.

8You shall not do as we are doing here today, each man whatever is right in his own eyes,

9for you have not yet come to the rest and to the inheritance that the LORD your God is giving you.

10But when you cross the Jordan and live in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to inherit, and He gives you rest from all your enemies around you, and you live in safety,

11then to the place that the LORD your God will choose, to make His name dwell there — there you shall bring all that I command you: your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and the contribution of your hand, and all your choice vows that you vow to the LORD.

12You shall rejoice before the LORD your God, you and your sons and your daughters, your male slaves and your female slaves, and the Levite who is inside your gates, since he has no share or inheritance with you.

13Guard yourself so that you do not offer your burnt offerings in every place that you see,

14but in the place that the LORD will choose in one of your tribes, there you shall offer your burnt offerings, and there you shall do all that I command you.

Meat in Your Towns

15Yet you may slaughter and eat meat in any of your towns, as much as you desire, according to the blessing of the LORD your God that He has given you. The unclean and the clean may eat of it, as of the gazelle and the deer.

16Only the blood you shall not eat; pour it out on the ground like water.

17You may not eat within your towns the tithe of your grain or of your new wine or of your oil, or the firstborn of your herd or of your flock, or any of your vows that you vow, or your freewill offerings, or the contribution of your hand.

18Rather, you shall eat them before the LORD your God in the place that the LORD your God will choose, you and your son and your daughter, your male slave and your female slave, and the Levite who is inside your gates, and you shall rejoice before the LORD your God in all that you put your hand to.

19Guard yourself so that you do not forsake the Levite as long as you live on your ground.

20When the LORD your God enlarges your border, as He has promised you, and you say, 'Let me eat meat,' because you long to eat meat, you may eat meat as much as you desire.

21If the place that the LORD your God will choose to put His name there is too far from you, you may slaughter from your herd and from your flock that the LORD has given you, as I have commanded you, and you may eat within your towns as much as you desire.

22Just as the gazelle and the deer are eaten, so you may eat it; the unclean and the clean alike may eat it.

23Only be firm not to eat the blood, for the blood is the life, and you shall not eat the life with the meat.

24You shall not eat it; pour it out on the ground like water.

25You shall not eat it, so that it may go well with you and with your sons after you, when you do what is right in the eyes of the LORD.

26Only your holy things that you have, and your vows, you shall take up and go to the place that the LORD will choose.

27You shall offer your burnt offerings, the meat and the blood, on the altar of the LORD your God. The blood of your sacrifices shall be poured out on the altar of the LORD your God, and the meat you may eat.

28Keep and listen to all these words that I command you, so that it may go well with you and with your sons after you forever, when you do what is good and right in the eyes of the LORD your God.

Do Not Ask About Their Gods

29When the LORD your God cuts off before you the nations whom you are going in to dispossess, and you dispossess them and live in their land,

30guard yourself so that you are not snared into following them, after they have been destroyed before you, and so that you do not inquire about their gods, saying, 'How did these nations serve their gods? I too will do the same.'

31You shall not do so to the LORD your God, for every detestable thing that the LORD hates they have done for their gods. They even burn their sons and their daughters in the fire to their gods.

32Every word that I command you, you shall be careful to do. You shall not add to it, and you shall not take away from it.

Notes

  • v4 "You shall not do so to the LORD your God" — not a ban on destroying His altars, but on worshipping Him the way the nations worshipped theirs: in any place, on every hill (v2). The same words return in v31.

  • v5 "the place that the LORD your God will choose… to put His name there" — the phrase recurs through the chapter (vv5, 11, 14, 18, 21, 26) and never names the place. Deuteronomy looks ahead to one sanctuary without saying where.

  • v8 "each man whatever is right in his own eyes" — ish kol ha-yashar be-einav. Judges ends on the same phrase (Judges 21:25) for a time with no king. Here it describes Israel in the wilderness.

  • v15 "as of the gazelle and the deer" — game animals, clean to eat but never offered on the altar. Meat from the herd, when slaughtered far from the altar, is to be treated the same way: eaten anywhere, by anyone, pure or not.

  • vv15–16, 20–25 meat away from the altar — Leviticus 17:3–4 had required every ox or sheep or goat slaughtered, in the camp or outside it, to be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting. With one distant place of sacrifice, Deuteronomy allows slaughter at home. Only the blood keeps its rule.

  • v23 "for the blood is the life" — ki ha-dam hu ha-nefesh, as in Leviticus 17:11, For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and Genesis 9:4, flesh with its soul — its blood — you shall not eat. Nefesh is soul and life at once.

  • v31 "They even burn their sons and their daughters in the fire" — the practice Leviticus 18:21 forbids by name: You shall not give any of your children to pass over to Molech.

  • v32 "You shall not add to it, and you shall not take away from it" — as in 4:2. The Hebrew counts this verse as 13:1.
