chapters.title: If a Prophet Arises
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 13

The Prophet Whose Sign Comes True

1If a prophet or a dreamer of dreams arises among you and gives you a sign or a wonder,

2and the sign or the wonder that he spoke to you comes true, and he says, 'Let us go after other gods' — gods you have not known — 'and let us serve them,'

3you shall not listen to the words of that prophet or that dreamer of dreams. For the LORD your God is testing you, to know whether you love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul.

4After the LORD your God you shall walk, and Him you shall fear. His commandments you shall keep, and His voice you shall listen to. Him you shall serve, and to Him you shall hold fast.

5That prophet or that dreamer of dreams shall be put to death, because he has spoken rebellion against the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slaves, to push you off the way in which the LORD your God commanded you to walk. So you shall purge the evil from among you.

The One Who Entices You in Secret

6If your brother, your mother's son, or your son or your daughter, or the wife of your embrace, or your friend who is as your own soul entices you in secret, saying, 'Let us go and serve other gods' — gods that neither you nor your fathers have known,

7from the gods of the peoples who are around you, near you or far from you, from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth —

8you shall not consent to him or listen to him. Your eye shall not pity him; you shall not spare him and you shall not cover for him.

9You shall surely kill him. Your hand shall be the first against him to put him to death, and afterward the hand of all the people.

10You shall stone him, and he shall die, because he sought to push you away from the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slaves.

11All Israel shall hear and be afraid, and no one among you will again do anything like this evil thing.

A Town That Turns Away

12If you hear it said of one of your towns that the LORD your God is giving you to live in,

13'Worthless men have gone out from among you and pushed the inhabitants of their town away, saying, "Let us go and serve other gods," gods you have not known,'

14you shall inquire and search and ask thoroughly. If it is true and the thing is certain, that this detestable thing has been done among you,

15you shall surely strike the inhabitants of that town with the sword, devoting it to destruction, with all that is in it and its animals, with the sword.

16You shall gather all its spoil into the middle of its open square, and burn the town and all its spoil with fire, whole, to the LORD your God. It shall be a heap forever; it shall not be built again.

17None of what is devoted to destruction shall cling to your hand, so that the LORD may turn from the heat of His anger and give you compassion, and have compassion on you and multiply you, as He swore to your fathers,

18when you listen to the voice of the LORD your God, keeping all His commandments that I command you today, doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD your God.

Notes

  • vv1–3 the sign that comes true — a true sign does not make a true prophet. The test is not what he can do but where he leads: after other gods. A fulfilled wonder is itself called a test, from God.

  • v4 "After the LORD your God you shall walk" — six verbs in a row, each with the LORD placed first for weight: walk, fear, keep, listen, serve, hold fast.

  • v5 "So you shall purge the evil from among you" — u-vi'arta ha-ra mi-qirbekha, you shall burn out the evil. Bi'er is the verb of fire consuming. The formula returns nine times in Deuteronomy's laws, from here to 24:7.

  • v6 "the wife of your embrace… your friend who is as your own soul" — the list moves inward: brother, child, wife, the friend closest of all. The nearer the voice, the stronger the pull, and the law names each.

  • v13 "Worthless men" — benei veliyya'al, sons of worthlessness. The phrase becomes a stock insult in the historical books.

  • v14 "inquire and search and ask thoroughly" — three verbs and an adverb before anything is done: the town is not destroyed on a rumor (v12, if you hear it said).

  • v16 "whole, to the LORD your God" — kalil, the word for the priest's grain offering that goes up entire (Leviticus 6:22–23). The whole town is burned as if it were an offering.

chapters.title: Clean and Unclean, and the Tithe
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 14

Sons of the LORD

1You are sons of the LORD your God. You shall not gash yourselves or make a bald patch between your eyes for the dead,

2for you are a holy people to the LORD your God, and the LORD has chosen you to be a people for His own treasure, out of all the peoples who are on the face of the ground.

What You May Eat

3You shall not eat any detestable thing.

4These are the animals you may eat: the ox, the sheep and the goat,

5the deer, the gazelle, the roebuck, the wild goat, the ibex, the antelope and the mountain sheep.

6Any animal that has a divided hoof, split in two, and brings up the cud among the animals, you may eat.

7But you shall not eat these, among those that bring up the cud or have a divided hoof, split: the camel, the hare and the rock badger, because they bring up the cud but do not have a divided hoof — they are unclean for you;

8and the pig, because it has a divided hoof but does not bring up the cud — it is unclean for you. You shall not eat their flesh, and you shall not touch their carcasses.

9Of all that is in the water you may eat these: anything that has fins and scales you may eat.

10Anything that does not have fins and scales you shall not eat. It is unclean for you.

11Every clean bird you may eat.

12These are the ones you shall not eat: the eagle, the bearded vulture, the black vulture,

13the buzzard, the falcon, and the kite of every kind,

14every kind of raven,

15the ostrich, the nighthawk, the gull, and the hawk of every kind,

16the owl, the great owl, the white owl,

17the pelican, the carrion vulture, the cormorant,

18the stork, the heron of every kind, the hoopoe, and the bat.

19Every winged swarming thing is unclean for you; they shall not be eaten.

20Every clean winged creature you may eat.

21You shall not eat any animal that has died on its own. You may give it to the guest who is inside your gates, and he may eat it, or you may sell it to a foreigner, for you are a holy people to the LORD your God. You shall not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.

The Tithe

22You shall surely tithe all the yield of your seed that comes out of the field year by year.

23You shall eat before the LORD your God, in the place that He will choose to make His name dwell there, the tithe of your grain, your new wine and your oil, and the firstborn of your herd and of your flock, so that you may learn to fear the LORD your God all the days.

24If the way is too long for you, so that you are not able to carry it, because the place that the LORD your God will choose to put His name there is too far from you, when the LORD your God blesses you,

25then you shall turn it into silver, bind up the silver in your hand, and go to the place that the LORD your God will choose.

26Spend the silver on whatever you desire: on cattle or sheep, on wine or strong drink, on whatever your soul asks of you. Eat there before the LORD your God and rejoice, you and your household.

27The Levite who is inside your gates — do not forsake him, for he has no share or inheritance with you.

28At the end of three years you shall bring out all the tithe of your yield in that year and lay it up inside your gates.

29The Levite, because he has no share or inheritance with you, and the guest, the orphan and the widow who are inside your gates shall come and eat and be satisfied, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hand that you do.

Notes

  • v1 "You are sons of the LORD your God" — the reason given for not cutting the body in mourning. Leviticus 19:28 and 21:5 forbid the same gashes and bald patches; here the ground is sonship.

  • v3 "any detestable thing" — to'evah, the word used of idols in 7:25–26, now of food. The list that follows spells out what counts.

  • vv4–5 ten clean animals — three from the herd and flock, seven wild. Several of the seven Hebrew names (yachmur, dishon, te'o, zemer) occur only here or once more, and the English names are the usual identifications, not certainties.

  • vv7–8 — the list of Leviticus 11:4–8, in shorter form; the hare comes before the rock badger here.

  • v13 "the buzzard" — ha-ra'ah, a word found only here. Leviticus 11:14 has ha-da'ah in the same place; in Hebrew letters ר and ד differ by one small stroke, and many take this for the same bird. Deuteronomy's list also has ha-dayyah, the kite, which Leviticus lacks.

  • v21 "You may give it to the guest… or sell it to a foreigner" — Leviticus 17:15 held the ger who ate such meat to the same washing as the native. Deuteronomy's reason for Israel's abstaining is holiness: for you are a holy people.

  • v21 "You shall not boil a young goat in its mother's milk" — the third time, after Exodus 23:19 and 34:26, and each time it closes a passage.

  • vv22–27 the tithe eaten at the feast — Numbers 18:21 gave the tithe to the Levites. Here the family eats it at the chosen place, with the Levite as guest, and may even turn it into silver and buy wine or strong drink there. The two laws have been read as two different tithes.

  • vv28–29 the third-year tithe — stored in the towns for those without land: the Levite, the guest, the orphan and the widow.

chapters.title: The Year of Release
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 15

The Release of Debts

1At the end of every seven years you shall make a release.

2This is the manner of the release: every creditor shall release what he has lent to his neighbor. He shall not press his neighbor, his brother, for payment, because the LORD's release has been proclaimed.

3From the foreigner you may press for payment, but whatever of yours is with your brother, your hand shall release.

4Yet there will be no needy among you — for the LORD will surely bless you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance to possess —

5if only you listen, listen to the voice of the LORD your God, to be careful to do all this commandment that I command you today.

6For the LORD your God will bless you, as He promised you. You will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow; you will rule over many nations, but they will not rule over you.

Open Your Hand

7If there is among you a needy man, one of your brothers, in any of your towns in your land that the LORD your God is giving you, you shall not harden your heart or shut your hand against your needy brother.

8Rather, you shall open, open your hand to him, and lend, lend him enough for his need, whatever he lacks.

9Guard yourself so that there is not a worthless thought in your heart, saying, 'The seventh year, the year of release, is near,' and your eye is evil toward your needy brother and you give him nothing. He will cry to the LORD against you, and it will be sin in you.

10You shall give, give to him, and your heart shall not be evil when you give to him, because for this thing the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and in all that you put your hand to.

11For the needy will never cease from the land. That is why I command you, saying, 'You shall open, open your hand to your brother, to your poor and to your needy in your land.'

Freeing a Hebrew Slave

12If your brother, a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman, is sold to you, he shall serve you six years, and in the seventh year you shall send him away from you free.

13When you send him away from you free, you shall not send him away empty-handed.

14You shall load, load him from your flock, from your threshing floor and from your winepress. As the LORD your God has blessed you, you shall give to him.

15Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt and the LORD your God redeemed you. That is why I command you this thing today.

16And it shall come to pass, if he says to you, 'I will not go out from you,' because he loves you and your household, since it is good for him with you,

17then you shall take an awl and put it through his ear into the door, and he shall be your slave forever. To your female slave also you shall do the same.

18It shall not seem hard in your eyes when you send him away from you free, for he has served you six years, worth twice the wages of a hired man. The LORD your God will bless you in all that you do.

19Every firstborn male that is born in your herd and in your flock you shall consecrate to the LORD your God. You shall not work with the firstborn of your ox, and you shall not shear the firstborn of your flock.

20Before the LORD your God you shall eat it, year by year, in the place that the LORD will choose, you and your household.

  • vv4 and 11 "no needy among you… the needy will never cease from the land" — not a contradiction but two sides of one law: poverty need not exist if the command is kept (vv4–5), and since it will not be kept perfectly, the hand must stay open (v11).   • vv8, 10, 11, 14 "open, open… lend, lend… give, give… load, load" — the verbs are doubled each time, the Hebrew way of pressing hard.

  • v9 "a worthless thought" — davar… veliyya'al, the word of worthless men in 13:13. The creditor who refuses a loan because the release is near is doing the same kind of thing as the man who leads a town astray.

  • v12 "a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman" — Exodus 21:2–11 treats the female slave by a separate law; Deuteronomy frees her on the same terms as the man (v17).

chapters.title: Three Times a Year
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 16

Passover and Unleavened Bread

1Keep the month of Aviv, and make the Passover to the LORD your God, for in the month of Aviv the LORD your God brought you out of Egypt by night.

2You shall sacrifice the Passover to the LORD your God, from the flock and the herd, in the place that the LORD will choose to make His name dwell there.

3You shall not eat anything leavened with it. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread with it, the bread of affliction — for in haste you came out of the land of Egypt — so that you may remember the day you came out of the land of Egypt all the days of your life.

4No leaven shall be seen with you in all your territory for seven days, and none of the meat that you sacrifice in the evening on the first day shall remain overnight until morning.

5You may not sacrifice the Passover within any of your towns that the LORD your God is giving you,

6but at the place that the LORD your God will choose to make His name dwell there, there you shall sacrifice the Passover, in the evening, as the sun goes down, at the time you came out of Egypt.

7You shall cook it and eat it in the place that the LORD your God will choose, and in the morning you shall turn and go to your tents.

8Six days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a closing assembly to the LORD your God; you shall do no work.

The Festival of Weeks

9You shall count seven weeks for yourself. From the time the sickle is first put to the standing grain you shall begin to count seven weeks.

10Then you shall keep the Festival of Weeks to the LORD your God, with a freewill offering from your hand, which you shall give as the LORD your God blesses you.

11You shall rejoice before the LORD your God, you and your son and your daughter, your male slave and your female slave, the Levite who is inside your gates, and the guest, the orphan and the widow who are among you, in the place that the LORD your God will choose to make His name dwell there.

12Remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and be careful to do these statutes.

The Festival of Booths

13You shall keep the Festival of Booths seven days, when you gather in from your threshing floor and from your winepress.

14You shall rejoice in your festival, you and your son and your daughter, your male slave and your female slave, the Levite and the guest, the orphan and the widow who are inside your gates.

15Seven days you shall keep the festival to the LORD your God in the place that the LORD will choose, for the LORD your God will bless you in all your yield and in all the work of your hands, and you shall be nothing but joyful.

16Three times in the year all your males shall appear before the face of the LORD your God in the place that He will choose: at the Festival of Unleavened Bread, at the Festival of Weeks, and at the Festival of Booths. They shall not appear before the face of the LORD empty-handed,

17each with the gift of his hand, according to the blessing of the LORD your God that He has given you.

Judges and Officials

18Judges and officials you shall appoint for yourself in all your towns that the LORD your God is giving you, tribe by tribe, and they shall judge the people with righteous judgment.

19You shall not bend judgment. You shall not show partiality, and you shall not take a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of the righteous.

20Justice, justice you shall pursue, so that you may live and possess the land that the LORD your God is giving you.

21You shall not plant for yourself a sacred pole, any tree, beside the altar of the LORD your God that you make for yourself.

22You shall not set up for yourself a standing stone, which the LORD your God hates.

Notes

  • v1 "by night" — Exodus 12:31 has Pharaoh call for Moses at night, and Numbers 33:3 has Israel set out on the day after the Passover. The night is when the release was won.

  • v2 "from the flock and the herd" — Exodus 12:5 takes the Passover animal from the sheep or from the goats; Deuteronomy allows cattle for the Passover sacrifice and moves it from the household to the chosen place (vv5–6).

  • v3 "the bread of affliction" — lechem 'oni, from the same 'oni as the affliction of My people in Exodus 3:7. Unleavened bread is poor people's bread, and bread made in a hurry.

  • v7 "You shall cook it" — u-vishshalta, the verb Exodus 12:9 used when it forbade the lamb boiled at all in water. Here it may mean simply cook. 2 Chronicles 35:13 puts the two together: they cooked the Passover in the fire.

  • v8 "a closing assembly" — atseret, as at the end of Booths in Leviticus 23:36.

  • v9 "seven weeks" — counted from the first cutting of the grain, not from a fixed date as in Leviticus 23:15. Leviticus 23:16 counts fifty days; from the Greek word for fiftieth comes the festival's later name, Pentecost.

  • vv11, 14 the guest, the orphan and the widow — the festivals are not for the landowner's household alone. Those who own no land are named each time.

  • v19 "a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise" — Exodus 23:8 has the clear-sighted, piqchim; Deuteronomy has chakhamim, the wise. The warning holds even for the best judge.

  • v20 "Justice, justice you shall pursue" — tsedeq tsedeq tirdof, the noun doubled for emphasis.

  • vv21–22 sacred pole and standing stone — the objects that 7:5 and 12:3 ordered torn down among the nations are not to be set up beside God's own altar either.

chapters.title: The Judge and the King
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 17

No Blemished Offering

1You shall not sacrifice to the LORD your God an ox or a sheep that has a blemish, any bad thing, for that is detestable to the LORD your God.

On the Word of Two Witnesses

2If there is found among you, in any of your towns that the LORD your God is giving you, a man or a woman who does what is evil in the eyes of the LORD your God, transgressing His covenant,

3and has gone and served other gods and bowed down to them, or to the sun or the moon or any of the host of heaven, which I have not commanded,

4and it is told to you and you hear of it, then you shall inquire thoroughly. If it is true and the thing is certain, that this detestable thing has been done in Israel,

5you shall bring out that man or that woman who has done this evil thing to your gates — the man or the woman — and stone them, and they shall die.

6On the word of two witnesses or three witnesses the one who is to die shall be put to death. He shall not be put to death on the word of one witness.

7The hand of the witnesses shall be the first against him to put him to death, and afterward the hand of all the people. So you shall purge the evil from among you.

The Case Too Hard for You

8If a case is too hard for you in judgment — between blood and blood, between claim and claim, between mark and mark — matters of dispute within your towns, then you shall get up and go up to the place that the LORD your God will choose.

9You shall come to the Levitical priests and to the judge who is in office in those days, and inquire, and they will declare to you the word of judgment.

10You shall do according to the word that they declare to you from that place that the LORD will choose, and you shall be careful to do all that they instruct you.

11According to the instruction that they teach you, and according to the judgment that they tell you, you shall do. You shall not turn aside from the word that they declare to you, to the right or to the left.

12The man who acts presumptuously, not listening to the priest who stands there to serve the LORD your God, or to the judge, that man shall die. So you shall purge the evil from Israel.

13All the people shall hear and be afraid, and will not act presumptuously again.

The King

14When you come into the land that the LORD your God is giving you, and possess it and live in it, and you say, 'Let me set a king over me, like all the nations that are around me,'

15you shall surely set over you a king whom the LORD your God will choose. From among your brothers you shall set a king over you; you may not put over you a foreigner, who is not your brother.

16Only, he shall not multiply horses for himself, nor make the people return to Egypt in order to multiply horses, since the LORD has said to you, 'You shall never again return that way.'

17He shall not multiply wives for himself, so that his heart does not turn aside, and silver and gold he shall not greatly multiply for himself.

18And it shall come to pass, when he sits on the throne of his kingdom, he shall write for himself a copy of this instruction in a book, from what is before the Levitical priests.

19It shall be with him, and he shall read in it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the LORD his God, to keep all the words of this instruction and these statutes, to do them,

20so that his heart is not lifted up above his brothers, and so that he does not turn aside from the commandment, to the right or to the left, so that he may prolong his days in his kingdom, he and his sons, in Israel.

Notes

  • v1 "a blemish" — mum, as in 15:21 and Leviticus 22:20. A defective animal offered to God is to'evah, the same word used of idols.

  • v4 "If it is true and the thing is certain" — the words of 13:14, where a whole town was on trial. The same care is demanded for one person.

  • v6 "two witnesses or three witnesses" — repeated as a general rule in 19:15. Jesus cites that verse in Matthew 18:16.

  • v7 "The hand of the witnesses shall be the first" — the one who testifies must also be the first to act on his testimony. False witness would make him the killer.

  • v8 "between blood and blood… claim and claim… mark and mark" — cases of killing, of property, and of nega, the mark of blight that the priest judges in Leviticus 13.

  • v11 "to the right or to the left" — the phrase returns in v20 for the king: he too may not turn aside from the instruction.

  • v14 "like all the nations that are around me" — the words the elders use in 1 Samuel 8:5: set a king over us to judge us, like all the nations.

  • vv16–17 horses, wives, silver and gold — three things the king may not multiply. 1 Kings records Solomon importing horses from Egypt (10:28), and seven hundred wives who turned his heart (11:3).

  • v18 "a copy of this instruction" — mishneh ha-torah ha-zot. The Greek reads to deuteronomion touto, this second law, which gave the book its Greek and English name (see the note on 1:1).

  • v20 "so that his heart is not lifted up above his brothers" — the king is still a brother (v15), and the book in his hand is the same one the people keep.

chapters.title: A Prophet Like Me
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 18

The Portion of the Priests and Levites

1The Levitical priests, all the tribe of Levi, shall have no share or inheritance with Israel. They shall eat the LORD's offerings by fire, His inheritance.

2They shall have no inheritance among their brothers; the LORD is their inheritance, as He said to them.

3This shall be the priests' due from the people, from those who offer a sacrifice, whether ox or sheep: they shall give the priest the shoulder, the two cheeks and the stomach.

4The first of your grain, your new wine and your oil, and the first of the shearing of your flock, you shall give him.

5For the LORD your God has chosen him out of all your tribes, to stand to serve in the name of the LORD, him and his sons, all the days.

6If a Levite comes from any of your towns in all Israel where he lives as a guest, and comes with all the desire of his soul to the place that the LORD will choose,

7he may serve in the name of the LORD his God like all his brothers the Levites who stand there before the LORD.

8They shall eat equal portions, besides what he receives from the sale of his fathers' goods.

Not Like the Nations

9When you come into the land that the LORD your God is giving you, you shall not learn to do according to the detestable things of those nations.

10There shall not be found among you anyone who makes his son or his daughter pass through the fire, a soothsayer, one who reads omens, one who practices divination, or a sorcerer,

11or one who casts spells, or one who asks a ghost or a spirit, or one who seeks out the dead.

12For whoever does these things is detestable to the LORD, and because of these detestable things the LORD your God is driving them out from before you.

13You shall be whole with the LORD your God.

14For these nations that you are dispossessing listen to those who read omens and to soothsayers. But as for you, the LORD your God has not given you this.

A Prophet Like Me

15A prophet from among you, from your brothers, like me, the LORD your God will raise up for you. To him you shall listen —

16just as you asked of the LORD your God at Horeb on the day of the assembly, saying, 'Let me not hear again the voice of the LORD my God, and let me not see this great fire any more, or I will die.'

17The LORD said to me, 'They have spoken well in what they have spoken.

18A prophet I will raise up for them from among their brothers, like you, and I will put My words in his mouth, and he shall speak to them all that I command him.

19And it shall come to pass that whoever will not listen to My words that he speaks in My name, I Myself will require it of him.

20But the prophet who presumes to speak a word in My name that I have not commanded him to speak, or who speaks in the name of other gods, that prophet shall die.'

21If you say in your heart, 'How shall we know the word that the LORD has not spoken?' —

22when a prophet speaks in the name of the LORD, and the word does not happen and does not come true, that is the word that the LORD has not spoken. The prophet has spoken it presumptuously. You shall not be afraid of him.

Notes

  • v3 "the shoulder, the two cheeks and the stomach" — a different list from the breast that is waved and the thigh that is lifted off of Leviticus 7:34, given from the peace offerings. Deuteronomy's portions come from any sacrifice of ox or sheep.

  • vv6–8 the Levite from the towns — with sacrifice only at the chosen place, a Levite living in the towns may come and serve there as an equal.

  • vv10–11 the list — seven practices, gathering words used elsewhere one or two at a time: mekhashef, sorcerer, as Exodus 22:18; ov and yidde'oni, a ghost or a spirit, as Leviticus 19:31 and 20:27; me'onen and menachesh, reads omens and practices divination, as Leviticus 19:26. Each is a way of learning or controlling what God has not said. Makes his son or his daughter pass through the fire heads the list, as in 12:31.

  • v13 "You shall be whole" — tamim, the word said of Noah (Genesis 6:9) and asked of Abram (Genesis 17:1, be whole). Of an animal it is without defect; of a person it is wholeness toward God, with nothing held back for omens and diviners.

  • v15 "A prophet… like me" — navi… kamoni. The promise answers v14: other nations listen to diviners; Israel will have a prophet. Peter reads it of Jesus in Acts 3:22, and Stephen quotes it in Acts 7:37.

  • v16 "Let me not hear again the voice of the LORD my God" — the people's plea at Sinai, Exodus 20:19: You speak with us, and we will listen. The prophet is God's answer to their own request (v17).

  • v19 "I Myself will require it of him" — anokhi edrosh me'immo: God Himself will hold to account whoever refuses the prophet's word.

  • vv20–22 the false prophet — 13:1–3 dealt with the prophet whose sign comes true but who leads to other gods; this is the prophet whose word does not come true. Either one fails.

A Prophet Like Me
A prophet from among you, from your brothers, like me, the LORD your God will raise up for you. To him you shall listen —
just as you asked of the LORD your God at Horeb on the day of the assembly, saying, 'Let me not hear again the voice of the LORD my God, and let me not see this great fire any more, or I will die.'
The LORD said to me, 'They have spoken well in what they have spoken.
A prophet I will raise up for them from among their brothers, like you, and I will put My words in his mouth, and he shall speak to them all that I command him.
And it shall come to pass that whoever will not listen to My words that he speaks in My name, I Myself will require it of him.
But the prophet who presumes to speak a word in My name that I have not commanded him to speak, or who speaks in the name of other gods, that prophet shall die.'
If you say in your heart, 'How shall we know the word that the LORD has not spoken?' —

when a prophet speaks in the name of the LORD, and the word does not happen and does not come true, that is the word that the LORD has not spoken. The prophet has spoken it presumptuously. You shall not be afraid of him.

chapters.title: Towns of Refuge
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 19

Three Towns in the Land

1When the LORD your God cuts off the nations whose land the LORD your God is giving you, and you dispossess them and live in their towns and in their houses,

2you shall set apart three towns for yourself within your land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.

3You shall prepare the road for yourself, and divide into three parts the territory of your land that the LORD your God gives you as an inheritance, so that anyone who kills may flee there.

4This is the case of the one who kills who may flee there and live: whoever strikes his neighbor unintentionally, without having hated him before —

5as when a man goes into the forest with his neighbor to cut wood, and his hand swings the axe to cut down the tree, and the iron slips from the handle and strikes his neighbor so that he dies — he may flee to one of these towns and live.

6Otherwise the avenger of blood, pursuing the one who killed while his heart is hot, may overtake him because the way is long, and strike him dead, though he did not deserve to die, since he had not hated him before.

7That is why I command you, saying, 'You shall set apart three towns for yourself.'

8If the LORD your God enlarges your territory, as He swore to your fathers, and gives you all the land that He promised to give to your fathers —

9if you are careful to do all this commandment that I command you today, to love the LORD your God and to walk in His ways all the days — then you shall add three more towns for yourself to these three,

10so that innocent blood is not shed within your land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and so blood guilt is not on you.

11But if a man hates his neighbor and lies in wait for him, and rises against him and strikes him dead, and he flees to one of these towns,

12the elders of his town shall send and take him from there and give him into the hand of the avenger of blood, and he shall die.

13Your eye shall not pity him. You shall purge the innocent blood from Israel, and it will go well with you.

The Boundary Marker

14You shall not move your neighbor's boundary marker, which the men of old set, in your inheritance that you will inherit in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.

Witnesses

15A single witness shall not rise against a man for any guilt or any sin, in any sin that he sins. On the word of two witnesses or on the word of three witnesses a matter shall stand.

16If a violent witness rises against a man to testify against him of wrongdoing,

17then both men who have the dispute shall stand before the LORD, before the priests and the judges who are in office in those days.

18The judges shall inquire thoroughly, and if the witness is a false witness who has testified falsely against his brother,

19you shall do to him as he planned to do to his brother. So you shall purge the evil from among you.

20The rest shall hear and be afraid, and they will never again do anything like this evil thing among you.

21Your eye shall not pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

Notes

  • vv2–3 three towns in the land — Moses has already set apart three beyond the Jordan (4:41–43); these are the three in the land of Canaan of Numbers 35:14. Prepare the road so that no one is too far from one.

  • v4 "without having hated him before" — mi-temol shilshom, from yesterday and the day before: no history of hatred. The same test as 4:42.

  • v5 the axe — the law gives one plain case instead of a definition: the iron slips from the handle. Anyone can see that no one meant it.

  • v6 "while his heart is hot" — the avenger is not blamed for his anger; the town of refuge exists because anger will not stop to ask.

  • vv8–9 three more towns — if the land grows to the full promise. Joshua 20:7–8 names six towns in all, three on each side of the Jordan; the further three are never named.

  • v13 "purge the innocent blood from Israel" — the formula of 13:5, with innocent blood for the evil. Numbers 35:33: blood pollutes the land.

  • v14 "which the men of old set" — rishonim, the first ones. Moving a boundary stone steals land quietly, from people who cannot see it happen; Proverbs 22:28 repeats the command.

  • v15 "a matter shall stand" — the rule of 17:6 widened from capital cases to any guilt or any sin. Matthew 18:16 quotes it: every matter may be established by the mouth of two or three witnesses.

  • v16 "a violent witness" — ed chamas, the word of the flood, the earth was filled with violence (Genesis 6:11). False testimony is violence done with words.

  • vv19, 21 "as he planned to do to his brother… eye for eye" — the false witness receives what his lie would have done. The list here matches Exodus 21:23–24; Jesus quotes Eye for eye, and tooth for tooth in Matthew 5:38.

chapters.title: When You Go Out to War
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 20

Do Not Be Afraid

1When you go out to battle against your enemies and see horses and chariots, a people greater than you, you shall not be afraid of them, for the LORD your God is with you, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.

2And it shall come to pass, when you draw near to the battle, the priest shall come forward and speak to the people.

3He shall say to them, 'Hear, Israel: you are drawing near today to battle against your enemies. Do not let your heart be faint. Do not be afraid, do not panic, and do not tremble before them,

4for the LORD your God is the one who goes with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.'

Who Goes Home

5The officials shall speak to the people, saying, 'Who is the man who has built a new house and has not dedicated it? Let him go and return to his house, or he may die in the battle and another man dedicate it.

6Who is the man who has planted a vineyard and has not yet used its fruit? Let him go and return to his house, or he may die in the battle and another man use its fruit.

7Who is the man who is engaged to a woman and has not taken her? Let him go and return to his house, or he may die in the battle and another man take her.'

8The officials shall speak further to the people and say, 'Who is the man who is afraid and faint of heart? Let him go and return to his house, so that he does not make his brothers' hearts melt like his own.'

9And it shall come to pass, when the officials have finished speaking to the people, they shall appoint commanders of the armies at the head of the people.

Cities Far and Near

10When you draw near to a city to fight against it, you shall call out to it for peace.

11And it shall come to pass, if it answers you with peace and opens to you, all the people found in it shall be forced labor for you and shall serve you.

12But if it does not make peace with you and makes war against you, you shall besiege it.

13When the LORD your God gives it into your hand, you shall strike all its males with the sword.

14Only the women, the little ones, the animals and all that is in the city, all its spoil, you shall take as plunder for yourself, and you shall eat the spoil of your enemies that the LORD your God has given you.

15So you shall do to all the cities that are very far from you, which are not of the cities of these nations here.

16But of the cities of these peoples that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, you shall not let anything that breathes live.

17You shall devote them to destruction — the Hittite and the Amorite, the Canaanite and the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite — as the LORD your God has commanded you,

18so that they do not teach you to do according to all their detestable things that they have done for their gods, and so sin against the LORD your God.

The Trees of the Field

19When you besiege a city for many days, fighting against it to take it, you shall not destroy its trees by swinging an axe against them. You may eat from them, but you shall not cut them down. Is the tree of the field a man, that it should go into the siege before you?

20Only the trees that you know are not trees for food you may destroy and cut down, and build siege works against the city that is making war with you, until it falls.

Notes

  • v1 "horses and chariots" — what Egypt had at the Sea of Reeds (Exodus 14). Who brought you up from the land of Egypt is the reason not to fear them.

  • v2 "the priest shall come forward" — the first voice before a battle is not a commander's but a priest's, and his message is Hear, Israel, the opening of 6:4.

  • vv5–7 house, vineyard, bride — three beginnings not yet enjoyed. A man is sent home rather than die and leave the first use to another. The newly married man appears again in 24:5.

  • v6 "has not yet used its fruit" — lo chillelo, has not made it common. Leviticus 19:23–25 kept the fruit of a new tree from ordinary eating until the fifth year; the verb here is the release of the fruit for ordinary eating.

  • v8 "afraid and faint of heart" — fear spreads: so that he does not make his brothers' hearts melt, the word the spies used in 1:28.

  • vv10–18 two kinds of cities — a city far away is first offered peace. The cities of the seven nations are devoted to destruction (7:2), and the reason given is worship: so that they do not teach you.

  • v19 "Is the tree of the field a man" — ki ha-adam ets ha-sadeh. The fruit tree cannot run from the army and is not the enemy. The same words can be read as a statement, for the tree of the field is man's life, and older translations divided on it.

chapters.title: Blood in the Field
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 21

The Unsolved Killing

1If someone is found slain on the ground that the LORD your God is giving you to possess, lying in the field, and it is not known who struck him,

2your elders and your judges shall go out and measure the distance to the towns that are around the slain man.

3And it shall come to pass that the town nearest to the slain man — the elders of that town shall take a heifer from the herd that has not been worked and has not pulled in a yoke.

4The elders of that town shall bring the heifer down to a valley with a flowing stream, which is neither plowed nor sown, and there in the valley they shall break the heifer's neck.

5The priests, the sons of Levi, shall come forward, for the LORD your God has chosen them to serve Him and to bless in the name of the LORD, and by their word every dispute and every mark shall be settled.

6All the elders of that town nearest to the slain man shall wash their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the valley,

7and they shall answer and say, 'Our hands did not shed this blood, and our eyes did not see it.

8Make atonement, LORD, for Your people Israel, whom You redeemed, and do not set innocent blood among Your people Israel.' So the blood shall be atoned for them.

9So you shall purge the innocent blood from among you, when you do what is right in the eyes of the LORD.

The Captive Woman

10When you go out to battle against your enemies, and the LORD your God gives them into your hand and you take them captive,

11and you see among the captives a woman beautiful in form, and you set your heart on her and would take her as your wife,

12you shall bring her into your house, and she shall shave her head and do her nails.

13She shall take off the clothing of her captivity and live in your house, and weep for her father and her mother a full month. After that you may go in to her and be her husband, and she shall be your wife.

14And it shall come to pass, if you no longer delight in her, you shall let her go wherever she wishes. You shall certainly not sell her for silver; you shall not treat her as a slave, because you have violated her.

The Firstborn's Right

15If a man has two wives, one loved and the other hated, and both the loved and the hated have borne him sons, and the firstborn son is the hated one's,

16then on the day he gives his sons what he has as an inheritance, he may not make the son of the loved wife firstborn in place of the son of the hated wife, who is the firstborn.

17He shall acknowledge the firstborn, the son of the hated wife, by giving him a double portion of all that he has, for he is the first of his vigor; the right of the firstborn is his.

The Rebellious Son

18If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son who does not listen to the voice of his father or the voice of his mother, and they discipline him but he will not listen to them,

19his father and his mother shall take hold of him and bring him out to the elders of his town, to the gate of his place.

20They shall say to the elders of his town, 'This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious. He will not listen to our voice. He is a glutton and a drunkard.'

21All the men of his town shall stone him, and he shall die. So you shall purge the evil from among you, and all Israel shall hear and be afraid.

The Body on the Tree

22If a man has committed a sin deserving death and he is put to death, and you hang him on a tree,

23his body shall not remain overnight on the tree. You shall surely bury him that same day, for one who is hanged is a curse of God. You shall not make unclean your ground that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.

Notes

  • vv1–9 the unsolved killing — no one can be punished, but the blood cannot be left (19:10, so blood guilt is not on you). The nearest town takes responsibility. The heifer that has not been worked dies in a valley neither plowed nor sown: untouched life, untouched land.

  • v4 "break the heifer's neck" — arafu, the verb used for the unredeemed donkey in Exodus 13:13, you shall break its neck. It is not a sacrifice; there is no altar and no blood on one.

  • v6 "wash their hands" — a sign of innocence spoken aloud in v7. Pilate does the same in Matthew 27:24, he took water and washed his hands… saying, "I am innocent of this man's blood."

  • vv10–14 the captive woman — she mourns a full month before any marriage. If she is later sent away, she goes free: you shall not treat her as a slave.

  • v14 "because you have violated her" — 'innitah, the verb used of Shechem in Genesis 34:2, violated her. Having taken her, the man has lost the right to sell her.

  • v15 "one loved and the other hated" — the words of Genesis 29:30–31, Leah was hated. Jacob gave Joseph, son of the loved Rachel, one shoulder above your brothers (Genesis 48:22). 1 Chronicles 5:1 says Reuben lost the birthright for his own sin, not his mother's place; this law forbids a father to choose by love alone.

  • v17 "the first of his vigor" — reshit ono, as Jacob calls Reuben in Genesis 49:3: my strength and the first of my vigor. A double portion, pi shenayim, a mouth of two, is what Elisha asks of Elijah's spirit in 2 Kings 2:9.

  • v20 "a glutton and a drunkard" — zolel ve-sove. Jesus says He was called a glutton and a drunkard in Matthew 11:19.

  • v23 "one who is hanged is a curse of God" — qilelat Elohim talui. The body was hung up after death as a warning, and taken down before night. Paul quotes the verse in its Greek form in Galatians 3:13: Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree.

chapters.title: Your Brother's Ox
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 22

Do Not Look Away

1You shall not see your brother's ox or his sheep straying and hide yourself from them. You shall surely bring them back to your brother.

2If your brother is not near you, or you do not know him, you shall bring it into your house, and it shall stay with you until your brother seeks it, and you shall give it back to him.

3So you shall do with his donkey, so you shall do with his cloak, and so you shall do with anything your brother loses that you find. You may not hide yourself.

4You shall not see your brother's donkey or his ox fallen on the road and hide yourself from them. You shall surely help him lift them up.

Laws of Order

5A woman shall not wear a man's gear, and a man shall not put on a woman's cloak, for whoever does these things is detestable to the LORD your God.

6If you come upon a bird's nest on the road, in any tree or on the ground, with young ones or eggs, and the mother sitting on the young or on the eggs, you shall not take the mother with the young.

7You shall surely let the mother go, and the young you may take for yourself, so that it may go well with you and you may prolong your days.

8When you build a new house, you shall make a parapet for your roof, so that you do not bring blood on your house if anyone falls from it.

9You shall not sow your vineyard with two kinds of seed, or the whole yield will become holy — the seed you have sown and the produce of the vineyard.

10You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey together.

11You shall not wear mixed cloth, wool and linen together.

12You shall make tassels for yourself on the four corners of your garment with which you cover yourself.

The Slandered Bride

13If a man takes a wife and goes in to her, and then hates her,

14and makes charges against her and brings out a bad name on her, saying, 'I took this woman, and when I came near her I did not find in her the signs of virginity,'

15then the girl's father and her mother shall take the signs of the girl's virginity and bring them out to the elders of the town at the gate.

16The girl's father shall say to the elders, 'I gave my daughter to this man as his wife, and he hates her.

17He has made charges against her, saying, "I did not find in your daughter the signs of virginity." But these are the signs of my daughter's virginity.' They shall spread the cloth before the elders of the town.

18The elders of that town shall take the man and discipline him.

19They shall fine him a hundred pieces of silver and give them to the girl's father, because he has brought out a bad name on a virgin of Israel. She shall remain his wife; he may not send her away all his days.

20But if the thing is true, and the signs of virginity were not found in the girl,

21they shall bring the girl out to the entrance of her father's house, and the men of her town shall stone her, and she shall die, because she has done an outrage in Israel, whoring in her father's house. So you shall purge the evil from among you.

Adultery and Rape

22If a man is found lying with a woman married to a husband, both of them shall die, the man who lay with the woman and the woman. So you shall purge the evil from Israel.

23If a girl who is a virgin is engaged to a man, and a man finds her in the town and lies with her,

24you shall bring them both out to the gate of that town and stone them, and they shall die — the girl because she did not cry out in the town, and the man because he violated his neighbor's wife. So you shall purge the evil from among you.

25But if the man finds the engaged girl in the field, and the man seizes her and lies with her, then only the man who lay with her shall die.

26To the girl you shall do nothing; there is in the girl no sin deserving death. For this case is like a man who rises against his neighbor and murders him:

27he found her in the field; the engaged girl cried out, and there was no one to save her.

28If a man finds a girl who is a virgin, who is not engaged, and seizes her and lies with her, and they are found,

29the man who lay with her shall give the girl's father fifty pieces of silver, and she shall be his wife, because he has violated her. He may not send her away all his days.

30A man shall not take his father's wife, and he shall not uncover his father's skirt.

Notes

  • vv1–4 "hide yourself" — hit'allamta, make yourself not see. Exodus 23:4–5 commanded the same for your enemy's ox and the one who hates you; here the animal is your brother's, and the law names the temptation: looking away.

  • v6 "you shall not take the mother with the young" — and the reward is the same as for honoring father and mother (5:16, so that your days may be long, and so that it may go well with you): the smallest command carries the promise of the greatest.

  • v8 "a parapet for your roof" — flat roofs were used as living space. A householder who leaves the edge open is responsible for the fall: blood on your house.

  • vv9–11 two kinds — Leviticus 19:19 forbade sowing a field with two kinds and wearing a garment woven of two kinds of material. Here sha'atnez, mixed cloth, is defined: wool and linen together. Become holy means forfeit to the sanctuary.

  • v12 "tassels" — gedilim, twisted cords, a different word from the tsitsit of Numbers 15:38, tassels on the corners of their garments, but the same command.

  • v21 "an outrage in Israel" — nevalah, the word said of Shechem in Genesis 34:7, he had done an outrage in Israel.

  • vv23–27 the town and the field — the law judges by what the girl could do. In the town a cry would have been heard; in the field there was no one to save her, and she is treated as one who was attacked, like a murder victim (v26).

  • vv28–29 the girl not engaged — Exodus 22:16–17 has the same case: payment to the father and marriage, which the father may refuse. Deuteronomy fixes the payment and forbids the man ever to divorce her.

  • v30 "uncover his father's skirt" — kenaf aviv, his father's wing, the edge of the garment. The same law as Leviticus 18:8, You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's wife. The Hebrew counts this verse as 23:1.

speech.text: Deuteronomy 22
Do Not Look Away
You shall not see your brother's ox or his sheep straying and hide yourself from them. You shall surely bring them back to your brother.
If your brother is not near you, or you do not know him, you shall bring it into your house, and it shall stay with you until your brother seeks it, and you shall give it back to him.
So you shall do with his donkey, so you shall do with his cloak, and so you shall do with anything your brother loses that you find. You may not hide yourself.
You shall not see your brother's donkey or his ox fallen on the road and hide yourself from them. You shall surely help him lift them up.
Laws of Order
A woman shall not wear a man's gear, and a man shall not put on a woman's cloak, for whoever does these things is detestable to the LORD your God.
If you come upon a bird's nest on the road, in any tree or on the ground, with young ones or eggs, and the mother sitting on the young or on the eggs, you shall not take the mother with the young.
You shall surely let the mother go, and the young you may take for yourself, so that it may go well with you and you may prolong your days.
When you build a new house, you shall make a parapet for your roof, so that you do not bring blood on your house if anyone falls from it.
You shall not sow your vineyard with two kinds of seed, or the whole yield will become holy — the seed you have sown and the produce of the vineyard.
You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey together.
You shall not wear mixed cloth, wool and linen together.
You shall make tassels for yourself on the four corners of your garment with which you cover yourself.
The Slandered Bride
If a man takes a wife and goes in to her, and then hates her,
and makes charges against her and brings out a bad name on her, saying, 'I took this woman, and when I came near her I did not find in her the signs of virginity,'
then the girl's father and her mother shall take the signs of the girl's virginity and bring them out to the elders of the town at the gate.
The girl's father shall say to the elders, 'I gave my daughter to this man as his wife, and he hates her.

He has made charges against her, saying, "I did not find in your daughter the signs of virginity." But these are the signs of my daughter's virginity.' They shall spread the cloth before the elders of the town.
The elders of that town shall take the man and discipline him.

They shall fine him a hundred pieces of silver and give them to the girl's father, because he has brought out a bad name on a virgin of Israel. She shall remain his wife; he may not send her away all his days.

they shall bring the girl out to the entrance of her father's house, and the men of her town shall stone her, and she shall die, because she has done an outrage in Israel, whoring in her father's house. So you shall purge the evil from among you.

If a man is found lying with a woman married to a husband, both of them shall die, the man who lay with the woman and the woman. So you shall purge the evil from Israel.
If a girl who is a virgin is engaged to a man, and a man finds her in the town and lies with her,

you shall bring them both out to the gate of that town and stone them, and they shall die — the girl because she did not cry out in the town, and the man because he violated his neighbor's wife. So you shall purge the evil from among you.
But if the man finds the engaged girl in the field, and the man seizes her and lies with her, then only the man who lay with her shall die.
To the girl you shall do nothing; there is in the girl no sin deserving death. For this case is like a man who rises against his neighbor and murders him:
he found her in the field; the engaged girl cried out, and there was no one to save her.
If a man finds a girl who is a virgin, who is not engaged, and seizes her and lies with her, and they are found,
the man who lay with her shall give the girl's father fifty pieces of silver, and she shall be his wife, because he has violated her. He may not send her away all his days.
A man shall not take his father's wife, and he shall not uncover his father's skirt.

chapters.title: The Assembly of the LORD
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 23

Who May Enter the Assembly

1No one whose testicles are crushed or whose male organ is cut off shall enter the assembly of the LORD.

2No one born of a forbidden union shall enter the assembly of the LORD; even to the tenth generation none of his shall enter the assembly of the LORD.

3No Ammonite or Moabite shall enter the assembly of the LORD; even to the tenth generation none of theirs shall enter the assembly of the LORD, forever,

4because they did not meet you with bread and water on the way when you came out of Egypt, and because they hired against you Balaam son of Beor from Pethor of Aram-naharaim, to curse you.

5But the LORD your God would not listen to Balaam, and the LORD your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, because the LORD your God loved you.

6You shall not seek their peace or their good all your days, forever.

7You shall not detest an Edomite, for he is your brother. You shall not detest an Egyptian, because you were a guest in his land.

8Children born to them in the third generation may enter the assembly of the LORD.

A Holy Camp

9When you go out as a camp against your enemies, you shall guard yourself from every bad thing.

10If there is among you a man who is not clean because of what happened in the night, he shall go outside the camp; he shall not come inside the camp.

11And it shall come to pass, toward evening, he shall bathe in water, and when the sun goes down he may come inside the camp.

12You shall have a place outside the camp, and you shall go out there.

13You shall have a spade among your gear, and when you sit down outside, you shall dig with it and turn back and cover your excrement.

14For the LORD your God walks about inside your camp, to deliver you and to give your enemies over before you. So your camp shall be holy, so that He does not see anything indecent among you and turn away from you.

Various Laws

15You shall not hand over to his master a slave who has escaped from his master to you.

16He shall live with you, among you, in the place that he chooses in one of your towns, wherever it is good for him. You shall not wrong him.

17There shall be no consecrated woman among the daughters of Israel, and there shall be no consecrated man among the sons of Israel.

18You shall not bring the wages of a prostitute or the price of a dog into the house of the LORD your God for any vow, for both of them are detestable to the LORD your God.

19You shall not charge interest to your brother, interest on silver, interest on food, interest on anything that is lent at interest.

20To a foreigner you may lend at interest, but to your brother you shall not lend at interest, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all that you put your hand to in the land that you are going into to possess.

21When you make a vow to the LORD your God, you shall not delay to pay it, for the LORD your God will surely require it of you, and it will be sin in you.

22But if you refrain from vowing, it will not be sin in you.

23What has come out of your lips you shall keep and do, just as you have vowed to the LORD your God a freewill offering that you have spoken with your mouth.

24When you go into your neighbor's vineyard, you may eat grapes until you are satisfied, as much as you wish, but you shall not put any in your basket.

25When you go into your neighbor's standing grain, you may pick the heads with your hand, but you shall not put a sickle to your neighbor's standing grain.

Notes

  • v2 "born of a forbidden union" — mamzer, a word found only here and in Zechariah 9:6. What union it means is not said; Jewish law later defined it as the child of adultery or incest.

  • vv3–5 Ammonite and Moabite — the reason is history, Numbers 22–24: Moab hired… Balaam. Nehemiah 13:1–2 reads this passage aloud to the returned exiles. Ruth, a Moabite woman, becomes David's great-grandmother (Ruth 4:17).

  • v5 "turned the curse into a blessing" — the story of Numbers 23–24 in one line: every time Balaam opened his mouth to curse, blessing came out.

  • v7 "for he is your brother… because you were a guest in his land" — Edom is Esau. Egypt enslaved Israel, yet Israel is not to detest it, because it first gave them a place to live.

  • v10 "what happened in the night" — miqreh laylah, an emission of semen, as Leviticus 15:16: he shall bathe his whole body in water, and be unclean until evening.

  • v14 "the LORD your God walks about inside your camp" — mit'hallekh, the verb of God walking about in the garden in Genesis 3:8. The camp must be clean because God is in it.

  • vv15–16 the escaped slave — he is not returned. He chooses where to live, and you shall not wrong him: tonennu, the verb of the command about the guest in Exodus 22:21, You shall not wrong a guest.

  • v17 "consecrated woman… consecrated man" — qedeshah and qadesh, the word Hirah uses in Genesis 38:21 for the woman Judah met. What the qedeshah did is disputed; the law here only bans it.

  • v18 "the price of a dog" — mechir kelev. Set beside the wages of a prostitute, most take dog to mean a male prostitute, the qadesh of v17.

  • v25 "you may pick the heads with your hand" — what the disciples do in Matthew 12:1, they began to pick heads of grain and eat them. The Pharisees' complaint there is the sabbath, not theft.

chapters.title: Remember That You Were a Slave
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 24

A Certificate of Divorce

1When a man takes a wife and marries her, and it comes to pass that she finds no favor in his eyes because he has found something indecent in her, and he writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hand and sends her out of his house,

2and she leaves his house and goes and becomes another man's wife,

3and the second man hates her and writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hand and sends her out of his house, or the second man who took her as his wife dies,

4then her first husband, who sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife after she has been made unclean, for that is detestable before the LORD. You shall not bring sin on the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.

5When a man takes a new wife, he shall not go out with the army, and no duty shall be laid on him. He shall be free at home one year and make the wife he has taken happy.

Pledges and Persons

6No one shall take a mill or an upper millstone in pledge, for he would be taking a life in pledge.

7If a man is found stealing a person from among his brothers, the sons of Israel, and treats him as a slave or sells him, that thief shall die. So you shall purge the evil from among you.

8Take care in a mark of blight to be very careful to do according to all that the Levitical priests teach you. As I commanded them, so you shall be careful to do.

9Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on the way when you came out of Egypt.

10When you make your neighbor a loan of any kind, you shall not go into his house to take his pledge.

11You shall stand outside, and the man to whom you are lending shall bring the pledge out to you.

12If he is a poor man, you shall not sleep in his pledge.

13You shall surely return the pledge to him when the sun goes down, so that he may sleep in his cloak and bless you. It will be righteousness for you before the LORD your God.

Wages, Justice, Gleanings

14You shall not exploit a hired man who is poor and needy, whether one of your brothers or one of your guests who are in your land inside your gates.

15You shall give him his wages on his day, before the sun goes down on it, for he is poor and sets his heart on it. Otherwise he will cry to the LORD against you, and it will be sin in you.

16Fathers shall not be put to death for sons, and sons shall not be put to death for fathers; each shall be put to death for his own sin.

17You shall not bend the judgment of the guest or the orphan, and you shall not take a widow's garment in pledge.

18Remember that you were a slave in Egypt and the LORD your God redeemed you from there. That is why I command you to do this thing.

19When you reap your harvest in your field and forget a sheaf in the field, you shall not go back to get it. It shall be for the guest, the orphan and the widow, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.

20When you beat your olive trees, you shall not go over the branches after you. It shall be for the guest, the orphan and the widow.

21When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, you shall not glean after you. It shall be for the guest, the orphan and the widow.

22Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt. That is why I command you to do this thing.

Notes

  • v1 "something indecent" — ervat davar, the phrase of 23:14, anything indecent in the camp. What it covers here was argued over: the Mishnah (Gittin 9:10) records that the school of Shammai read it as unfaithfulness and the school of Hillel as almost anything. Matthew 19:7 has the Pharisees ask, Why then did Moses command us to give a certificate of divorce?

  • vv1–4 one law, not a command to divorce — the whole passage is a single case, and its only ruling is v4: the first husband may not take her back. The certificate protects the woman: it proves she is free to marry again.

  • v5 "make the wife he has taken happy" — ve-simmach et ishto. The year at home is for her joy, and 20:7 already sent the engaged man home from battle.

  • v6 "a mill or an upper millstone" — the household's means of making bread each day. To take it in pledge is to take a life, nefesh.

  • v7 "stealing a person" — gonev nefesh, the law of Exodus 21:16, Whoever steals a man and sells him… shall be put to death.

  • vv8–9 "a mark of blight… Miriam" — nega ha-tsara'at, the priests' teaching of Leviticus 13–14. Miriam is the example: Miriam was blighted, white as snow (Numbers 12:10), after she spoke against Moses.

  • vv10–13 the pledge — the lender may not enter the borrower's house to choose his pledge. Exodus 22:26–27 already required a cloak taken in pledge to be returned before the sun goes down… In what shall he sleep?

  • vv14–15 the hired man's wages — Leviticus 19:13: The wages of a hired man shall not stay with you overnight until morning. He sets his heart on it: he has nothing else that day.

  • v16 "each shall be put to death for his own sin" — 2 Kings 14:6 quotes this verse: King Amaziah spared the sons of his father's murderers.

  • vv19–21 sheaf, olives, grapes — Leviticus 19:9–10 left the edges and gleanings for the poor and for the guest. Deuteronomy adds the forgotten sheaf, and names the guest, the orphan and the widow three times.

chapters.title: Remember Amalek
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 25

Forty Blows

1If there is a dispute between men and they come to judgment, and the judges judge them, declaring the righteous one righteous and the wicked one wicked,

2and it comes to pass, if the wicked one deserves to be beaten, the judge shall make him lie down and have him beaten in his presence with the number of blows his wickedness deserves.

3Forty blows he may give him, and no more, or if he goes on to beat him with more blows than these, your brother would be degraded in your eyes.

4You shall not muzzle an ox while it is threshing.

The Brother's Duty

5If brothers live together and one of them dies and has no son, the wife of the dead man shall not marry outside the family to a stranger. Her husband's brother shall go in to her and take her as his wife and do the brother's duty by her.

6And it shall come to pass that the firstborn whom she bears shall carry on the name of his dead brother, so that his name is not wiped out of Israel.

7But if the man does not wish to take his brother's wife, then his brother's wife shall go up to the gate, to the elders, and say, 'My husband's brother refuses to raise up a name for his brother in Israel; he will not do the brother's duty by me.'

8The elders of his town shall call him and speak to him. If he stands firm and says, 'I do not wish to take her,'

9then his brother's wife shall come up to him in the sight of the elders, pull his sandal off his foot, and spit in his face. She shall answer and say, 'So shall it be done to the man who will not build up his brother's house.'

10His name shall be called in Israel, 'The house of him whose sandal was pulled off.'

Various Laws

11When men fight together, a man and his brother, and the wife of one comes near to rescue her husband from the hand of the one striking him, and puts out her hand and seizes him by his private parts,

12you shall cut off her hand. Your eye shall not pity.

13You shall not have in your bag two kinds of weights, a large and a small.

14You shall not have in your house two kinds of ephah, a large and a small.

15A full and honest weight you shall have; a full and honest ephah you shall have, so that your days may be long on the ground that the LORD your God is giving you.

16For everyone who does these things, everyone who does injustice, is detestable to the LORD your God.

Remember Amalek

17Remember what Amalek did to you on the way when you came out of Egypt,

18how he met you on the way and cut off at your rear all who were lagging behind you, when you were faint and weary, and he did not fear God.

19And it shall come to pass, when the LORD your God has given you rest from all your enemies around you, in the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance to possess, you shall blot out the memory of Amalek from under the heavens. Do not forget.

Notes

  • vv1–3 forty blows — the limit protects the guilty man: your brother would be degraded. He is still your brother while he is being punished. Later practice stopped at thirty-nine to keep from going over; Paul says in 2 Corinthians 11:24, five times I received forty less one.

  • v4 "You shall not muzzle an ox while it is threshing" — the animal working the grain may eat from it. Paul quotes the verse in 1 Corinthians 9:9 for the right of those who work in the gospel to be supported.

  • vv5–10 "do the brother's duty" — yabbem, the word Judah uses to Onan in Genesis 38:8, do the brother's duty by her, and raise up seed for your brother. The Sadducees put this law to Jesus in Matthew 22:24.

  • v6 "carry on the name of his dead brother" — yaqum al shem achiv, stand on his brother's name. The child counts as the dead man's.

  • vv9–10 the sandal and the spit — the refusal is made public, and the man's household carries the name. Ruth 4:7 describes a sandal given over in a similar exchange of rights.

  • vv11–12 the wife's hand — mevushav, his private parts, from bosh, shame. The penalty is fixed and not to be softened: Your eye shall not pity, as for the murderer (19:13) and the false witness (19:21).

  • vv13–15 "two kinds of weights" — even va-even, a stone and a stone: one to buy with and one to sell with. Leviticus 19:36: You shall have honest scales, honest weights, an honest ephah.

  • vv17–19 Amalek — Exodus 17:8–16 tells the battle at Rephidim; Deuteronomy adds how Amalek fought: from behind, against the stragglers, when you were faint and weary. The command repeats God's own words in Exodus 17:14, I will utterly blot out the memory of Amalek from under the heavens, and ends with two words: lo tishkach, Do not forget.

chapters.title: A Wandering Aramean
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 26

The Basket of Firstfruits

1And it shall come to pass, when you come into the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and possess it and live in it,

2you shall take some of the first of all the fruit of the ground that you bring in from your land that the LORD your God is giving you, and put it in a basket, and go to the place that the LORD your God will choose to make His name dwell there.

3You shall come to the priest who is in office in those days and say to him, 'I declare today to the LORD your God that I have come into the land that the LORD swore to our fathers to give us.'

4The priest shall take the basket from your hand and set it down before the altar of the LORD your God.

5Then you shall answer and say before the LORD your God: 'A wandering Aramean was my father. He went down to Egypt and lived there as a guest, few in number, and there he became a nation, great, mighty and numerous.

6The Egyptians treated us badly and afflicted us and laid hard service on us.

7We cried to the LORD, the God of our fathers, and the LORD heard our voice and saw our affliction, our toil and our crushing.

8The LORD brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, with great terror, and with signs and wonders.

9He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.

10And now I have brought the first of the fruit of the ground that You, LORD, have given me.' You shall set it down before the LORD your God and bow down before the LORD your God.

11You shall rejoice in all the good that the LORD your God has given you and your household, you and the Levite and the guest who is among you.

The Third-Year Tithe

12When you have finished tithing all the tithe of your yield in the third year, the year of the tithe, and have given it to the Levite, the guest, the orphan and the widow, so that they may eat within your towns and be satisfied,

13you shall say before the LORD your God: 'I have removed the holy portion from my house, and I have also given it to the Levite and to the guest, to the orphan and to the widow, according to all Your commandment that You commanded me. I have not transgressed any of Your commandments, and I have not forgotten.

14I have not eaten of it in my mourning, I have not removed any of it while unclean, and I have not given any of it to the dead. I have listened to the voice of the LORD my God; I have done according to all that You commanded me.

15Look down from Your holy dwelling, from heaven, and bless Your people Israel and the ground that You have given us, as You swore to our fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey.'

You Have Declared, and He Has Declared

16This day the LORD your God commands you to do these statutes and rules. You shall be careful to do them with all your heart and with all your soul.

17You have declared today that the LORD is your God, and that you will walk in His ways and keep His statutes and His commandments and His rules, and listen to His voice.

18The LORD has declared today that you are a people for His own treasure, as He promised you, and that you are to keep all His commandments,

19and that He will set you high above all the nations that He has made, for praise and for a name and for glory, and that you shall be a holy people to the LORD your God, as He has spoken.

Notes

  • v5 "A wandering Aramean was my father" — arammi oved avi, three words. Oved is perishing, lost, straying, the verb of anything your brother loses in 22:3. The worshipper says my father, and then us: the story is told in the first person.

  • vv5–9 the confession — Israel's whole history before the land in five verses, from a lost man to a land of milk and honey, spoken over a basket of fruit. Nothing about Sinai is in it; the confession is about the gift of the land.

  • vv6–7 "afflicted us… our affliction… our crushing" — va-ye'annunu, the verb of Exodus 1:11, to afflict them with their burdens; 'onyenu, as in Exodus 3:7, I have seen the affliction of My people; lachatsenu, the crushing of Exodus 3:9.

  • v10 "the first of the fruit of the ground that You, LORD, have given me" — the speaker turns from telling God's deeds to addressing God directly.

  • vv13–14 the declaration of the tithe — I have removed, bi'arti, the verb of purge the evil: the holy portion is cleared out of the house as completely as evil is from Israel. Given any of it to the dead refers to offerings to the dead, or food for mourners (compare eaten of it in my mourning).

  • v15 "Look down from Your holy dwelling" — hashqifah, the verb of Genesis 18:16, where the men looked down over the face of Sodom before its judgment. Here the look that is asked for is blessing.

  • vv17–18 "You have declared… The LORD has declared" — he'emarta and he'emirkha, a form of amar, say, found only in these two verses. Each side has the other say what it will be: Israel says the LORD is its God, and the LORD says Israel is His people. It is the covenant in its simplest form.

  • v19 "a holy people" — the promise of Exodus 19:6, a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.
