chapters.title: Stones on Mount Ebal
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 27

Write the Instruction on Stones

1Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people, saying, "Keep all the commandment that I command you today.

2And it shall come to pass, on the day you cross the Jordan into the land that the LORD your God is giving you, you shall set up for yourself large stones and plaster them with plaster.

3You shall write on them all the words of this instruction when you cross over, so that you may enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you, a land flowing with milk and honey, as the LORD, the God of your fathers, has promised you.

4And it shall come to pass, when you have crossed the Jordan, you shall set up these stones, as I command you today, on Mount Ebal, and plaster them with plaster.

5There you shall build an altar to the LORD your God, an altar of stones. You shall not wield any iron tool on them.

6Of whole stones you shall build the altar of the LORD your God, and you shall offer burnt offerings on it to the LORD your God.

7You shall sacrifice peace offerings and eat there, and rejoice before the LORD your God.

8You shall write on the stones all the words of this instruction, making them very plain."

9Moses and the Levitical priests spoke to all Israel, saying, "Be silent and hear, Israel: this day you have become a people to the LORD your God.

10You shall listen to the voice of the LORD your God and do His commandments and His statutes that I command you today."

Blessing and Curse

11Moses commanded the people that day, saying,

12"These shall stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people when you have crossed the Jordan: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph and Benjamin.

13These shall stand on Mount Ebal for the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan and Naphtali.

14The Levites shall answer and say to every man of Israel in a loud voice:

15'Cursed is the man who makes a carved or cast image, detestable to the LORD, the work of a craftsman's hands, and sets it up in secret.' All the people shall answer and say, 'Amen.'

16'Cursed is he who dishonors his father or his mother.' All the people shall say, 'Amen.'

17'Cursed is he who moves his neighbor's boundary marker.' All the people shall say, 'Amen.'

18'Cursed is he who makes a blind man stray on the road.' All the people shall say, 'Amen.'

19'Cursed is he who bends the judgment of the guest, the orphan and the widow.' All the people shall say, 'Amen.'

20'Cursed is he who lies with his father's wife, for he has uncovered his father's skirt.' All the people shall say, 'Amen.'

21'Cursed is he who lies with any animal.' All the people shall say, 'Amen.'

22'Cursed is he who lies with his sister, his father's daughter or his mother's daughter.' All the people shall say, 'Amen.'

23'Cursed is he who lies with his mother-in-law.' All the people shall say, 'Amen.'

24'Cursed is he who strikes his neighbor in secret.' All the people shall say, 'Amen.'

25'Cursed is he who takes a bribe to strike down a life, innocent blood.' All the people shall say, 'Amen.'

26'Cursed is he who does not uphold the words of this instruction by doing them.' All the people shall say, 'Amen.'"

Notes

  • v1 "Moses and the elders of Israel" — here Moses commands together with the elders, and in v9 together with the priests. The speech is handing itself over to those who will remain after him.

  • vv2–4 plastered stones — the writing is on plaster laid over the stones, not carved into them. Joshua 8:32 tells of writing a copy of the instruction of Moses on stones there.

  • vv5–6 "You shall not wield any iron tool on them… whole stones" — the altar law of Exodus 20:25: you shall not build them cut — because you have waved your sword over it and profaned it. Whole, shelemot, is the root of the peace offerings, shelamim, of v7.

  • v8 "making them very plain" — ba'er heitev, the verb of 1:5, where Moses undertook to explain the instruction. The book ends as it began: the words are meant to be understood.

  • vv12–13 the tribes on the two mountains — the sons of Leah and Rachel stand for blessing; the sons of the servant women Bilhah and Zilpah, with Reuben and Zebulun, stand for the curse.

  • vv14–26 twelve curses, twelve Amens — each curse names something done where no judge would see: in secret (vv15, 24), to the blind, to the powerless, within the family. The people bind themselves with their own Amen to what no court could enforce.

  • v16 "dishonors" — maqleh, from qalal, to be light, the opposite of kabbed, honor, whose root means to be heavy (5:16).

  • v18 "makes a blind man stray" — Leviticus 19:14: you shall not put a stumbling block in front of a blind man.

  • v26 "does not uphold the words of this instruction" — Paul quotes the verse in Galatians 3:10 in its Greek form, which adds all: Cursed is everyone who does not remain in all the things written in the book of the Law, to do them.

chapters.title: Blessings and Curses
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 28

The Blessings

1And it shall come to pass, if you listen, listen to the voice of the LORD your God, to be careful to do all His commandments that I command you today, the LORD your God will set you high above all the nations of the earth.

2All these blessings will come on you and overtake you, if you listen to the voice of the LORD your God.

3Blessed are you in the city, and blessed are you in the field.

4Blessed is the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground and the fruit of your animals, the offspring of your cattle and the young of your flock.

5Blessed is your basket and your kneading bowl.

6Blessed are you when you come in, and blessed are you when you go out.

7The LORD will make your enemies who rise against you be struck down before you. They will come out against you one way and flee before you seven ways.

8The LORD will command the blessing to be with you in your barns and in all that you put your hand to, and He will bless you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.

9The LORD will establish you as a holy people for Himself, as He swore to you, if you keep the commandments of the LORD your God and walk in His ways.

10All the peoples of the earth will see that the name of the LORD is called over you, and they will be afraid of you.

11The LORD will make you abound in good, in the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your animals and the fruit of your ground, on the ground that the LORD swore to your fathers to give you.

12The LORD will open for you His good treasury, the heavens, to give the rain of your land in its season and to bless all the work of your hand. You will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow.

13The LORD will make you the head and not the tail; you will be only on top and not underneath, if you listen to the commandments of the LORD your God that I command you today, to keep and to do them,

14and do not turn aside from any of the words that I command you today, to the right or to the left, to go after other gods to serve them.

The Curses

15And it shall come to pass, if you do not listen to the voice of the LORD your God, to be careful to do all His commandments and His statutes that I command you today, all these curses will come on you and overtake you.

16Cursed are you in the city, and cursed are you in the field.

17Cursed is your basket and your kneading bowl.

18Cursed is the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground, the offspring of your cattle and the young of your flock.

19Cursed are you when you come in, and cursed are you when you go out.

20The LORD will send on you the curse, the confusion and the rebuke in all that you put your hand to and do, until you are destroyed and perish quickly, because of the evil of your deeds, because you have forsaken Me.

21The LORD will make the plague cling to you until He has finished you off the ground that you are going into to possess.

22The LORD will strike you with wasting disease and fever, inflammation and burning heat, with the sword, with scorching and with mildew, and they will pursue you until you perish.

23The heavens over your head will be bronze, and the earth under you iron.

24The LORD will make the rain of your land powder and dust; from the heavens it will come down on you until you are destroyed.

25The LORD will make you be struck down before your enemies. You will go out one way against them and flee seven ways before them, and you will be a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.

26Your dead body will be food for every bird of the heavens and for the beasts of the earth, and there will be no one to frighten them away.

27The LORD will strike you with the boils of Egypt, with tumors, with scabs and with itch, from which you cannot be healed.

28The LORD will strike you with madness and blindness and bewilderment of heart.

29You will grope at noon as the blind man gropes in darkness, and you will not prosper in your ways. You will be only oppressed and robbed all the days, and there will be no one to save you.

30You will be engaged to a woman, and another man will lie with her. You will build a house and not live in it. You will plant a vineyard and not use its fruit.

31Your ox will be slaughtered before your eyes, and you will not eat of it. Your donkey will be robbed from before your face and not come back to you. Your sheep will be given to your enemies, and there will be no one to save you.

32Your sons and your daughters will be given to another people, while your eyes look on and fail with longing for them all the day, and there will be nothing in the power of your hand.

33A people you have not known will eat the fruit of your ground and all your labor, and you will be only oppressed and crushed all the days.

34You will be driven mad by the sight your eyes see.

35The LORD will strike you with bad boils on the knees and on the legs, from which you cannot be healed, from the sole of your foot to the top of your head.

36The LORD will bring you and your king whom you set over you to a nation that neither you nor your fathers have known, and there you will serve other gods, wood and stone.

37You will become a horror, a proverb and a byword among all the peoples where the LORD drives you.

38You will carry much seed out to the field and gather in little, for the locust will consume it.

39You will plant vineyards and work them, but you will not drink the wine or gather the grapes, for the worm will eat them.

40You will have olive trees throughout all your territory, but you will not anoint yourself with oil, for your olives will drop off.

41You will father sons and daughters, but they will not be yours, for they will go into captivity.

42All your trees and the fruit of your ground the cricket will take over.

43The guest who is among you will rise above you higher and higher, and you will go down lower and lower.

44He will lend to you, but you will not lend to him. He will be the head, and you will be the tail.

45All these curses will come on you and pursue you and overtake you until you are destroyed, because you did not listen to the voice of the LORD your God, to keep His commandments and His statutes that He commanded you.

46They will be a sign and a wonder on you and on your seed forever.

A Nation from Far Away

47Because you did not serve the LORD your God with joy and gladness of heart for the abundance of everything,

48you will serve your enemies whom the LORD will send against you, in hunger and in thirst, in nakedness and in lack of everything. He will put an iron yoke on your neck until He has destroyed you.

49The LORD will bring against you a nation from far away, from the end of the earth, swooping as the eagle swoops, a nation whose language you will not understand,

50a nation hard of face, who will not lift the face of the old or show favor to the young.

51It will eat the fruit of your animals and the fruit of your ground until you are destroyed. It will leave you no grain, new wine or oil, no offspring of your cattle or young of your flock, until it has made you perish.

52It will besiege you in all your towns until your high and fortified walls, in which you trust, come down throughout all your land. It will besiege you in all your towns throughout all your land that the LORD your God has given you.

53You will eat the fruit of your womb, the flesh of your sons and your daughters whom the LORD your God has given you, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will distress you.

54The man who is most tender and delicate among you will look with an evil eye on his brother and on the wife of his embrace and on the last of his sons who remain,

55so as not to give any of them the flesh of his sons that he is eating, because nothing is left to him in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will distress you in all your towns.

56The woman who is most tender and delicate among you, who would not venture to set the sole of her foot on the ground for delicacy and tenderness, will look with an evil eye on the husband of her embrace and on her son and on her daughter,

57and on the afterbirth that comes out from between her feet and on her sons whom she bears, for she will eat them secretly for lack of everything, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will distress you in your towns.

Back to Egypt

58If you are not careful to do all the words of this instruction that are written in this book, to fear this glorious and awesome name, the LORD your God,

59then the LORD will make your blows and the blows of your seed extraordinary, great and lasting blows, and bad and lasting sicknesses.

60He will bring back on you all the diseases of Egypt that you were afraid of, and they will cling to you.

61Also every sickness and every blow that is not written in the book of this instruction, the LORD will bring on you until you are destroyed.

62You will be left few in number, where you were like the stars of the heavens for multitude, because you did not listen to the voice of the LORD your God.

63And it shall come to pass that as the LORD delighted over you to do you good and to multiply you, so the LORD will delight over you to make you perish and to destroy you, and you will be torn from the ground that you are going into to possess.

64The LORD will scatter you among all the peoples, from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth, and there you will serve other gods that neither you nor your fathers have known, wood and stone.

65Among those nations you will find no ease, and there will be no resting place for the sole of your foot. The LORD will give you there a trembling heart, failing eyes and a languishing soul.

66Your life will hang in doubt before you. You will be in dread night and day, and have no assurance of your life.

67In the morning you will say, 'If only it were evening!' and in the evening you will say, 'If only it were morning!' because of the dread of your heart that you will feel and the sight of your eyes that you will see.

68The LORD will bring you back to Egypt in ships, by a way of which I said to you, 'You will never see it again.' There you will offer yourselves for sale to your enemies as male and female slaves, and there will be no buyer.

Notes

  • vv3–6 and 16–19 six blessings, six curses — the same six lines, word for word, with Blessed turned to Cursed. City and field, womb and ground, basket and bowl, coming in and going out: the whole of life.

  • v10 "the name of the LORD is called over you" — shem YHWH niqra alekha, the phrase for ownership: what bears a name belongs to its owner.

  • vv13, 44 "the head and not the tail" — the blessing of v13 is turned against Israel in v44, where the guest becomes the head.

  • v22 "wasting disease and fever" — shachefet and qaddachat, the pair of Leviticus 26:16, wasting disease and fever. Scorching and mildew strike the grain.

  • v30 the three reversals — house, vineyard and bride, the three reasons for going home from war in 20:5–7, here each taken by another.

  • v49 "swooping as the eagle swoops… whose language you will not understand" — the invader is never named. Readers have seen Assyria and Babylon in it, and later Rome.

  • vv53–57 eating the children — the curse of Leviticus 26:29, You will eat the flesh of your sons, drawn out in horror. 2 Kings 6:28–29 and Lamentations 4:10 record it happening under siege.

  • v58 "this glorious and awesome name" — ha-shem ha-nikhbad ve-ha-nora ha-zeh: the Name standing for God Himself.

  • v63 "as the LORD delighted over you… so the LORD will delight" — the same verb, sas, both times, the boldest line in the chapter.

  • v68 "back to Egypt in ships" — the undoing of the exodus: back to the house of slaves, and not even wanted as slaves there.

Your ox will be slaughtered before your eyes, and you will not eat of it. Your donkey will be robbed from before your face and not come back to you. Your sheep will be given to your enemies, and there will be no one to save you.
Your sons and your daughters will be given to another people, while your eyes look on and fail with longing for them all the day, and there will be nothing in the power of your hand.
A people you have not known will eat the fruit of your ground and all your labor, and you will be only oppressed and crushed all the days.
You will be driven mad by the sight your eyes see.
The LORD will strike you with bad boils on the knees and on the legs, from which you cannot be healed, from the sole of your foot to the top of your head.
The LORD will bring you and your king whom you set over you to a nation that neither you nor your fathers have known, and there you will serve other gods, wood and stone.
You will become a horror, a proverb and a byword among all the peoples where the LORD drives you.
You will carry much seed out to the field and gather in little, for the locust will consume it.
You will plant vineyards and work them, but you will not drink the wine or gather the grapes, for the worm will eat them.
You will have olive trees throughout all your territory, but you will not anoint yourself with oil, for your olives will drop off.
You will father sons and daughters, but they will not be yours, for they will go into captivity.
All your trees and the fruit of your ground the cricket will take over.
The guest who is among you will rise above you higher and higher, and you will go down lower and lower.
He will lend to you, but you will not lend to him. He will be the head, and you will be the tail.

All these curses will come on you and pursue you and overtake you until you are destroyed, because you did not listen to the voice of the LORD your God, to keep His commandments and His statutes that He commanded you.
They will be a sign and a wonder on you and on your seed forever.
A Nation from Far Away
Because you did not serve the LORD your God with joy and gladness of heart for the abundance of everything,
you will serve your enemies whom the LORD will send against you, in hunger and in thirst, in nakedness and in lack of everything. He will put an iron yoke on your neck until He has destroyed you.
The LORD will bring against you a nation from far away, from the end of the earth, swooping as the eagle swoops, a nation whose language you will not understand,
a nation hard of face, who will not lift the face of the old or show favor to the young.

It will eat the fruit of your animals and the fruit of your ground until you are destroyed. It will leave you no grain, new wine or oil, no offspring of your cattle or young of your flock, until it has made you perish.

It will besiege you in all your towns until your high and fortified walls, in which you trust, come down throughout all your land. It will besiege you in all your towns throughout all your land that the LORD your God has given you.
You will eat the fruit of your womb, the flesh of your sons and your daughters whom the LORD your God has given you, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will distress you.
The man who is most tender and delicate among you will look with an evil eye on his brother and on the wife of his embrace and on the last of his sons who remain,
so as not to give any of them the flesh of his sons that he is eating, because nothing is left to him in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will distress you in all your towns.

The woman who is most tender and delicate among you, who would not venture to set the sole of her foot on the ground for delicacy and tenderness, will look with an evil eye on the husband of her embrace and on her son and on her daughter,

and on the afterbirth that comes out from between her feet and on her sons whom she bears, for she will eat them secretly for lack of everything, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy will distress you in your towns.
Back to Egypt
If you are not careful to do all the words of this instruction that are written in this book, to fear this glorious and awesome name, the LORD your God,
then the LORD will make your blows and the blows of your seed extraordinary, great and lasting blows, and bad and lasting sicknesses.
He will bring back on you all the diseases of Egypt that you were afraid of, and they will cling to you.
Also every sickness and every blow that is not written in the book of this instruction, the LORD will bring on you until you are destroyed.
You will be left few in number, where you were like the stars of the heavens for multitude, because you did not listen to the voice of the LORD your God.

And it shall come to pass that as the LORD delighted over you to do you good and to multiply you, so the LORD will delight over you to make you perish and to destroy you, and you will be torn from the ground that you are going into to possess.

The LORD will scatter you among all the peoples, from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth, and there you will serve other gods that neither you nor your fathers have known, wood and stone.
Among those nations you will find no ease, and there will be no resting place for the sole of your foot. The LORD will give you there a trembling heart, failing eyes and a languishing soul.
Your life will hang in doubt before you. You will be in dread night and day, and have no assurance of your life.

In the morning you will say, 'If only it were evening!' and in the evening you will say, 'If only it were morning!' because of the dread of your heart that you will feel and the sight of your eyes that you will see.

The LORD will bring you back to Egypt in ships, by a way of which I said to you, 'You will never see it again.' There you will offer yourselves for sale to your enemies as male and female slaves, and there will be no buyer.

chapters.title: The Covenant in Moab
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 29

1These are the words of the covenant that the LORD commanded Moses to make with the sons of Israel in the land of Moab, besides the covenant that He made with them at Horeb.

You Have Seen

2Moses called all Israel and said to them, "You have seen all that the LORD did before your eyes in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh and to all his servants and to all his land,

3the great trials that your eyes saw, the signs and those great wonders.

4Yet the LORD has not given you a heart to know, or eyes to see, or ears to hear, to this day.

5I have led you forty years in the wilderness. Your clothes have not worn out on you, and your sandal has not worn out on your foot.

6You have not eaten bread, and you have not drunk wine or strong drink, so that you may know that I am the LORD your God.

7When you came to this place, Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out against us to battle, and we struck them.

8We took their land and gave it as an inheritance to the Reubenites, to the Gadites and to the half-tribe of the Manassites.

9Keep the words of this covenant and do them, so that you may prosper in all that you do.

All of You, Today

10You are standing today, all of you, before the LORD your God — your heads, your tribes, your elders and your officials, every man of Israel,

11your little ones, your wives, and your guest who is inside your camp, from the one who cuts your wood to the one who draws your water —

12to enter into the covenant of the LORD your God and into His oath, which the LORD your God is making with you today,

13so that He may establish you today as His people, and He will be your God, as He promised you and as He swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob.

14Not with you alone am I making this covenant and this oath,

15but with whoever is standing here with us today before the LORD our God, and with whoever is not here with us today.

A Root Bearing Poison

16For you know how we lived in the land of Egypt, and how we passed through the nations that you passed through.

17You saw their loathsome things and their idols, wood and stone, silver and gold, that were among them.

18Let there not be among you a man or a woman, a family or a tribe, whose heart turns away today from the LORD our God to go and serve the gods of those nations. Let there not be among you a root bearing poison and wormwood,

19one who, when he hears the words of this oath, blesses himself in his heart, saying, 'I will have peace, though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart' — sweeping away the watered with the dry.

20The LORD will not be willing to forgive him. Then the anger of the LORD and His jealousy will smoke against that man, and every curse written in this book will settle on him, and the LORD will wipe out his name from under the heavens.

21The LORD will set him apart for evil out of all the tribes of Israel, according to all the curses of the covenant written in this book of the instruction.

What the Nations Will Say

22The generation to come, your sons who rise up after you, and the foreigner who comes from a far land, will say, when they see the blows of that land and the sicknesses with which the LORD has made it sick —

23all its land sulfur and salt, a burning, not sown, not sprouting, no grass growing on it, like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the LORD overthrew in His anger and His fury —

24all the nations will say, 'Why has the LORD done this to this land? What is this great burning anger?'

25They will say, 'Because they forsook the covenant of the LORD, the God of their fathers, which He made with them when He brought them out of the land of Egypt.

26They went and served other gods and bowed down to them, gods whom they had not known and whom He had not allotted to them.

27So the anger of the LORD burned against that land, to bring on it every curse written in this book.

28The LORD uprooted them from their ground in anger and in fury and in great wrath, and threw them into another land, as it is this day.'

29The hidden things belong to the LORD our God, but the revealed things belong to us and to our sons forever, to do all the words of this instruction.

Notes

  • v1 "besides the covenant that He made with them at Horeb" — the covenant in Moab is a second covenant alongside the first. The Hebrew counts this verse as 28:69, so 29:2–29 here is Hebrew 29:1–28.

  • v4 "Yet the LORD has not given you a heart to know" — the people saw everything and still did not understand. Paul uses this verse, blended with Isaiah 29:10, in Romans 11:8.

  • vv5–6 clothing, sandals, bread — 8:4 said the clothing did not wear out; here the sandals are added, and the speaker slips into God's own voice: so that you may know that I am the LORD your God.

  • v11 "from the one who cuts your wood to the one who draws your water" — the lowest labor in the camp. Joshua 9:21 gives these jobs to the Gibeonites.

  • vv14–15 "with whoever is not here with us today" — the covenant binds generations not yet born. The same point was made at Horeb in 5:3: but with us, we who are all here alive today.

  • v17 "their loathsome things and their idols" — shiqqutseihem, the fixed word loathsome; gillulim, idols, as in Leviticus 26:30, a word that may mean dung pellets in contempt.

  • v18 "a root bearing poison and wormwood" — rosh ve-la'anah, two bitter plants. Hebrews 12:15 takes up the image from the Greek: that no root of bitterness springing up cause trouble.

  • v19 "sweeping away the watered with the dry" — an obscure phrase, perhaps a proverb: the one man's hidden idolatry will bring down everyone, the green with the dry.

  • v23 "Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim" — the four cities of the plain named in Genesis 14:2. Genesis 19:24–25 tells how the LORD rained… sulfur and fire and overturned those cities; overthrow here is the same verb, haphakh.

  • v29 "The hidden things… the revealed things" — in the Hebrew text the words to us and to our sons carry dots written over each letter, one of the places in the Torah so marked by the scribes (the rabbis counted ten). What the dots were meant to signal was already debated in antiquity.

chapters.title: Choose Life
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 30

When You Return

1And it shall come to pass, when all these things come on you, the blessing and the curse that I have set before you, and you take them to heart among all the nations where the LORD your God has driven you,

2and you return to the LORD your God and listen to His voice according to all that I command you today, you and your sons, with all your heart and with all your soul,

3then the LORD your God will restore your fortunes and have compassion on you, and He will gather you again from all the peoples where the LORD your God has scattered you.

4If your outcasts are at the end of the heavens, from there the LORD your God will gather you, and from there He will take you.

5The LORD your God will bring you into the land that your fathers possessed, and you will possess it, and He will do you good and multiply you more than your fathers.

6The LORD your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your seed, to love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul, so that you may live.

7The LORD your God will put all these curses on your enemies and on those who hate you, who persecuted you.

8You will return and listen to the voice of the LORD and do all His commandments that I command you today.

9The LORD your God will make you abound in all the work of your hand, in the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your animals and the fruit of your ground, for good. For the LORD will again delight over you for good, as He delighted over your fathers,

10when you listen to the voice of the LORD your God, to keep His commandments and His statutes that are written in this book of the instruction, when you return to the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul.

Not Too Far Away

11For this commandment that I command you today is not too hard for you, and it is not far off.

12It is not in the heavens, that you should say, 'Who will go up for us to the heavens and bring it to us and let us hear it, so that we may do it?'

13Nor is it beyond the sea, that you should say, 'Who will cross over for us to the other side of the sea and bring it to us and let us hear it, so that we may do it?'

14For the word is very near you, in your mouth and in your heart, so that you can do it.

Life and Death

15See, I have set before you today life and good, and death and evil,

16in that I command you today to love the LORD your God, to walk in His ways and to keep His commandments and His statutes and His rules, so that you may live and multiply, and the LORD your God will bless you in the land that you are going into to possess.

17But if your heart turns away and you will not listen, and you are drawn away and bow down to other gods and serve them,

18I declare to you today that you will perish, perish. You will not prolong your days on the ground that you are crossing the Jordan to go into and possess.

19I call the heavens and the earth to witness against you today: I have set before you life and death, the blessing and the curse. Choose life, so that you may live, you and your seed,

20loving the LORD your God, listening to His voice and holding fast to Him — for He is your life and the length of your days — so that you may live on the ground that the LORD swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, to give them.

Notes

  • vv1–10 "return" — the verb shuv runs through the passage seven times: take them to heart (v1, bring back to your heart), you return (vv2, 8, 10), the LORD will restore your fortunes, shav et shevutkha (v3), gather you again, return and gather (v3), and will again delight (v9). When Israel turns back, God turns back.

  • v4 "at the end of the heavens" — bi-qtseh ha-shamayim: the horizon, the farthest edge anyone could be driven to.

  • v6 "The LORD your God will circumcise your heart" — in 10:16 the people were told, Circumcise, then, the foreskin of your heart. Here God promises to do it Himself.

  • v9 "delight over you for good, as He delighted over your fathers" — the verb sas of 28:63, where God would delight… to make you perish. The last word is not that one.

  • vv11–14 "not in the heavens… nor beyond the sea" — no hero needs to climb to heaven or cross the sea to fetch the commandment; it has already been given. Paul reads the verses of Christ in Romans 10:6–8, putting the abyss where the Hebrew has the sea, and ending with The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart.

  • v15 "life and good, and death and evil" — the pair of words from the tree of the knowing of good and evil (Genesis 2:9), now laid before Israel as a choice.

  • v19 "I call the heavens and the earth to witness" — as in 4:26. The witnesses will outlast the people who hear the words.

  • v20 "for He is your life" — ki hu chayyekha. What v19 asks Israel to choose is, in the end, God Himself.

chapters.title: Be Strong and Courageous
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 31

Joshua Will Cross Over

1Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel.

2He said to them, "I am a hundred and twenty years old today. I can no longer go out and come in, and the LORD has said to me, 'You shall not cross this Jordan.'

3The LORD your God Himself will cross over before you. He will destroy these nations before you, and you will dispossess them. Joshua is the one who will cross over before you, as the LORD has spoken.

4The LORD will do to them as He did to Sihon and to Og, the kings of the Amorites, and to their land, when He destroyed them.

5The LORD will give them over before you, and you shall do to them according to all the commandment that I have commanded you.

6Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or tremble before them, for the LORD your God is the one who goes with you. He will not let you go or forsake you."

7Then Moses called Joshua and said to him in the sight of all Israel, "Be strong and courageous, for you will go with this people into the land that the LORD swore to their fathers to give them, and you will cause them to inherit it.

8The LORD is the one who goes before you. He will be with you; He will not let you go or forsake you. Do not be afraid or lose heart."

Read It Every Seven Years

9Moses wrote this instruction and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and to all the elders of Israel.

10Moses commanded them, saying, "At the end of every seven years, at the set time of the year of release, at the Festival of Booths,

11when all Israel comes to appear before the face of the LORD your God in the place that He will choose, you shall read this instruction before all Israel in their hearing.

12Assemble the people, the men and the women and the little ones, and your guest who is inside your gates, so that they may hear and learn and fear the LORD your God, and be careful to do all the words of this instruction,

13and so that their sons, who have not known, may hear and learn to fear the LORD your God all the days that you live on the ground that you are crossing the Jordan to possess."

The Song as a Witness

14The LORD said to Moses, "The days are near for you to die. Call Joshua, and present yourselves in the tent of meeting, so that I may commission him." Moses and Joshua went and presented themselves in the tent of meeting.

15The LORD appeared in the tent in a pillar of cloud, and the pillar of cloud stood over the entrance of the tent.

16The LORD said to Moses, "You are about to lie down with your fathers, and this people will rise and give themselves to the foreign gods of the land they are going into, among them. They will forsake Me and break My covenant that I made with them.

17My anger will burn against them in that day. I will forsake them and hide My face from them, and they will be devoured, and many evils and troubles will find them. They will say in that day, 'Is it not because our God is not among us that these evils have found us?'

18I will surely hide My face in that day because of all the evil they have done, for they have turned to other gods.

19So now write this song for yourselves, and teach it to the sons of Israel. Put it in their mouths, so that this song may be a witness for Me against the sons of Israel.

20For when I bring them into the ground that I swore to their fathers, flowing with milk and honey, and they eat and are satisfied and grow fat, they will turn to other gods and serve them, and despise Me and break My covenant.

21And it shall come to pass, when many evils and troubles have found them, this song will testify before them as a witness, for it will not be forgotten from the mouths of their seed. For I know the shaping of their thoughts, what they are doing today, before I have brought them into the land that I swore."

22Moses wrote this song that day and taught it to the sons of Israel.

23He commissioned Joshua son of Nun and said, "Be strong and courageous, for you will bring the sons of Israel into the land that I swore to them, and I will be with you."

Beside the Ark

24When Moses had finished writing the words of this instruction in a book to the very end,

25Moses commanded the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, saying,

26"Take this book of the instruction and put it beside the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God, and let it be there as a witness against you.

27For I know your rebellion and your stiff neck. Even now, while I am still alive with you today, you have been rebellious against the LORD; how much more after my death!

28Assemble to me all the elders of your tribes and your officials, so that I may speak these words in their hearing and call the heavens and the earth to witness against them.

29For I know that after my death you will act corruptly and turn aside from the way that I have commanded you, and evil will meet you in the end of days, because you will do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD, provoking Him to anger with the work of your hands."

30Moses spoke in the hearing of all the assembly of Israel the words of this song, to the very end.

Notes

  • v2 "a hundred and twenty years old" — the limit of Genesis 6:3, his days shall be a hundred and twenty years. I can no longer go out and come in: yet 34:7 says his eye was not dim. The reason he stops is given in the same verse: You shall not cross this Jordan.

  • vv3, 8 "the one who goes before you" — Joshua crosses before the people (v3), but the LORD crosses before them first. The leader changes; the One who leads does not.

  • vv6, 8 "He will not let you go or forsake you" — lo yarpekha ve-lo ya'azvekha. Hebrews 13:5 quotes the promise: I will never leave you nor forsake you.

  • vv7, 23 "Be strong and courageous" — chazaq ve-emats, the words God commanded Moses to say in 3:28, strengthen him and encourage him. God says them again to Joshua in Joshua 1:6–9.

  • vv10–13 the reading every seven years — at the Festival of Booths of the year of release (15:1), everyone gathers, the men and the women and the little ones, and your guest, to hear the whole instruction read aloud.

  • v16 "You are about to lie down with your fathers" — hinnekha shokhev, God's announcement of what is about to happen. Lie down with your fathers is the idiom for death. Ve-zanah acharei, whore after, rendered give themselves to, is the word for prostitution: the turning to other gods is told as a wife's infidelity.

  • vv17–18 "hide My face" — hester panim, doubled in v18, I will surely hide My face. The people will conclude our God is not among us; the song will tell them why.

  • v21 "the shaping of their thoughts" — yitsro, his shaping, the word of Genesis 6:5 and 8:21, the shaping of the human heart is evil from his youth.

  • v26 "beside the ark" — the tablets are inside the ark (10:5); the book is kept beside it, as a witness against you.

  • v29 "in the end of days" — be-acharit ha-yamim, as in 4:30.

He said to them, "I am a hundred and twenty years old today. I can no longer go out and come in, and the LORD has said to me, 'You shall not cross this Jordan.'

The LORD will do to them as He did to Sihon and to Og, the kings of the Amorites, and to their land, when He destroyed them.
The LORD will give them over before you, and you shall do to them according to all the commandment that I have commanded you.
Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or tremble before them, for the LORD your God is the one who goes with you. He will not let you go or forsake you."

Then Moses called Joshua and said to him in the sight of all Israel, "Be strong and courageous, for you will go with this people into the land that the LORD swore to their fathers to give them, and you will cause them to inherit it.
The LORD is the one who goes before you. He will be with you; He will not let you go or forsake you. Do not be afraid or lose heart."
Read It Every Seven Years
Moses wrote this instruction and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and to all the elders of Israel.
Moses commanded them, saying, "At the end of every seven years, at the set time of the year of release, at the Festival of Booths,
when all Israel comes to appear before the face of the LORD your God in the place that He will choose, you shall read this instruction before all Israel in their hearing.

Assemble the people, the men and the women and the little ones, and your guest who is inside your gates, so that they may hear and learn and fear the LORD your God, and be careful to do all the words of this instruction,
and so that their sons, who have not known, may hear and learn to fear the LORD your God all the days that you live on the ground that you are crossing the Jordan to possess."
The Song as a Witness

The LORD said to Moses, "The days are near for you to die. Call Joshua, and present yourselves in the tent of meeting, so that I may commission him." Moses and Joshua went and presented themselves in the tent of meeting.
The LORD appeared in the tent in a pillar of cloud, and the pillar of cloud stood over the entrance of the tent.

The LORD said to Moses, "You are about to lie down with your fathers, and this people will rise and give themselves to the foreign gods of the land they are going into, among them. They will forsake Me and break My covenant that I made with them.

My anger will burn against them in that day. I will forsake them and hide My face from them, and they will be devoured, and many evils and troubles will find them. They will say in that day, 'Is it not because our God is not among us that these evils have found us?'
I will surely hide My face in that day because of all the evil they have done, for they have turned to other gods.
So now write this song for yourselves, and teach it to the sons of Israel. Put it in their mouths, so that this song may be a witness for Me against the sons of Israel.

For when I bring them into the ground that I swore to their fathers, flowing with milk and honey, and they eat and are satisfied and grow fat, they will turn to other gods and serve them, and despise Me and break My covenant.

And it shall come to pass, when many evils and troubles have found them, this song will testify before them as a witness, for it will not be forgotten from the mouths of their seed. For I know the shaping of their thoughts, what they are doing today, before I have brought them into the land that I swore."
Moses wrote this song that day and taught it to the sons of Israel.
He commissioned Joshua son of Nun and said, "Be strong and courageous, for you will bring the sons of Israel into the land that I swore to them, and I will be with you."
Beside the Ark
When Moses had finished writing the words of this instruction in a book to the very end,
Moses commanded the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, saying,
"Take this book of the instruction and put it beside the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God, and let it be there as a witness against you.
For I know your rebellion and your stiff neck. Even now, while I am still alive with you today, you have been rebellious against the LORD; how much more after my death!
Assemble to me all the elders of your tribes and your officials, so that I may speak these words in their hearing and call the heavens and the earth to witness against them.

For I know that after my death you will act corruptly and turn aside from the way that I have commanded you, and evil will meet you in the end of days, because you will do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD, provoking Him to anger with the work of your hands."
Moses spoke in the hearing of all the assembly of Israel the words of this song, to the very end.

chapters.title: The Song of Moses
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 32

The Song of Moses

1Give ear, heavens, and I will speak;
let the earth hear the words of my mouth.

2Let my teaching drop like the rain,
my speech distill like the dew,
like showers on the new grass,
like downpours on the plants.

3For I will proclaim the name of the LORD:
ascribe greatness to our God!

4The Rock — His work is whole,
for all His ways are justice.
A God of faithfulness and without wrong,
righteous and upright is He.

5They have acted corruptly toward Him;
they are not His sons, it is their blemish —
a crooked and twisted generation.

6Is this how you repay the LORD,
foolish and unwise people?
Is He not your Father, who acquired you,
who made you and established you?

7Remember the days of old;
consider the years of generation after generation.
Ask your father, and he will tell you,
your elders, and they will say to you.

8When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance,
when He divided the sons of man,
He set the boundaries of the peoples
according to the number of the sons of Israel.

9For the LORD's portion is His people,
Jacob the measured lot of His inheritance.

10He found him in a desert land,
in the empty howling waste.
He surrounded him, He cared for him,
He guarded him as the pupil of His eye.

11Like an eagle that stirs up its nest,
that hovers over its young,
He spread His wings, He took him,
He carried him on His pinions.

12The LORD alone led him,
and no foreign god was with him.

13He made him ride on the heights of the earth,
and he ate the produce of the field.
He made him suck honey from the rock
and oil from the flinty rock,

14curds of the herd and milk of the flock,
with the fat of lambs,
rams, the breed of Bashan, and goats,
with the fat of the kidneys of wheat —
and the blood of the grape you drank, foaming wine.

15Jeshurun grew fat and kicked —
you grew fat, you grew thick, you were gorged —
and he forsook God who made him
and scorned the Rock of his salvation.

16They made Him jealous with strange gods;
with detestable things they provoked Him.

17They sacrificed to demons, not God,
to gods they had not known,
new ones who came lately,
whom your fathers did not dread.

18You neglected the Rock who bore you,
and you forgot the God who brought you forth in labor.

19The LORD saw and spurned them,
provoked by His sons and His daughters.

20He said, 'I will hide My face from them;
I will see what their end will be,
for they are a perverse generation,
sons in whom there is no faithfulness.

21They made Me jealous with what is no god;
they provoked Me with their empty things.
So I will make them jealous with what is no people;
with a foolish nation I will provoke them.

22For a fire is kindled in My anger,
and it burns to the depths of Sheol;
it devours the earth and its yield
and sets on fire the foundations of the mountains.

23I will heap evils on them;
I will spend My arrows on them.

24Wasted with hunger, devoured by plague
and bitter destruction —
the teeth of beasts I will send against them,
with the venom of things that crawl in the dust.

25Outside the sword will bereave,
and inside the rooms, terror,
for young man and young woman alike,
the nursing child with the man of gray hair.

26I said, "I will cut them to pieces;
I will make their memory cease from among men,"

27had I not dreaded the provocation of the enemy,
that their adversaries might misunderstand,
that they might say, "Our hand is high,
and it was not the LORD who did all this."'

28For they are a nation void of counsel,
and there is no understanding in them.

29If they were wise, they would understand this;
they would discern their end.

30How could one chase a thousand,
and two put ten thousand to flight,
unless their Rock had sold them
and the LORD had given them up?

31For their rock is not like our Rock —
our enemies themselves are judges of it.

32For their vine is from the vine of Sodom
and from the fields of Gomorrah;
their grapes are grapes of poison,
their clusters are bitter.

33Their wine is the venom of serpents,
the cruel poison of vipers.

34'Is this not laid up in store with Me,
sealed up in My treasuries?

35Vengeance is Mine, and recompense,
for the time when their foot slips;
for the day of their calamity is near,
and what is prepared for them hurries on.'

36For the LORD will judge His people
and have compassion on His servants,
when He sees that their strength is gone
and there is none left, bond or free.

37He will say, 'Where are their gods,
the rock in which they took refuge,

38who ate the fat of their sacrifices
and drank the wine of their drink offering?
Let them rise up and help you;
let them be your shelter!

39See now that I, I am He,
and there is no god with Me.
I put to death and I make alive;
I wound and I heal,
and there is no one who can deliver from My hand.

40For I lift up My hand to heaven
and say: As I live forever,

41when I sharpen the lightning of My sword
and My hand takes hold of judgment,
I will return vengeance to My adversaries
and repay those who hate Me.

42I will make My arrows drunk with blood,
and My sword shall devour flesh —
with the blood of the slain and the captives,
from the long-haired heads of the enemy.'

43Rejoice, nations, with His people,
for He avenges the blood of His servants.
He returns vengeance to His adversaries
and makes atonement for His land, His people.

44Moses came and spoke all the words of this song in the hearing of the people, he and Hoshea son of Nun.

45When Moses had finished speaking all these words to all Israel,

46he said to them, "Set your hearts on all the words by which I warn you today, which you shall command your sons to be careful to do, all the words of this instruction.

47For it is no empty word for you; it is your life, and by this word you will prolong your days on the ground that you are crossing the Jordan to possess."

Go Up Mount Nebo

48The LORD spoke to Moses that very day, saying,

49"Go up this mountain of the Abarim, Mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab, opposite Jericho, and see the land of Canaan that I am giving to the sons of Israel as a possession.

50Die on the mountain that you are going up, and be gathered to your people, as Aaron your brother died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people,

51because you broke faith with Me among the sons of Israel at the waters of Meribah of Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin, because you did not show Me holy among the sons of Israel.

52For you shall see the land from a distance, but you shall not go there, into the land that I am giving to the sons of Israel."

Notes

  • v4 "The Rock" — ha-tsur, God's name five times in the song (vv4, 15, 18, 30, 31), set against their rock (vv31, 37). His work is whole: tamim, the word used of a person whole toward God (18:13).

  • v5 — the Hebrew is broken and hard to construe: corrupted to Him, not His sons, their blemish. Mum, blemish, is the fixed word for a defect in an offering.

  • v6 "Is He not your Father, who acquired you" — qanekha, the verb Eve uses in Genesis 4:1, I have gotten a man. One of the few places in the Torah where God is called Father.

  • v8 "according to the number of the sons of Israel" — so the Hebrew. The Greek reads according to the number of the angels of God: each nation given to a heavenly being, while the LORD's portion is His people (v9). A Hebrew fragment from Qumran is reported to read sons of God. Both readings are old; this rendering follows the Hebrew it translates.

  • v10 "the pupil of His eye" — ishon, the little man, the tiny figure one sees reflected in another's eye. Empty, tohu, is the word of Genesis 1:2, wild and waste.

  • v15 "Jeshurun" — Yeshurun, a name for Israel from yashar, upright, used here with irony: the upright one grew fat and kicked. It appears again in 33:5 and 33:26.

  • v18 "the God who brought you forth in labor" — mecholelekha, a verb of a mother's birth pains. The song gives God a father's name (v6) and a mother's labor.

  • v21 "no god… no people" — lo el… lo am: jealousy for jealousy, measure for measure. Paul quotes the second half in Romans 10:19, I will make you jealous by what is not a nation.

  • v35 "Vengeance is Mine" — li naqam ve-shillem. Paul quotes it in Romans 12:19 and Hebrews 10:30 has it with v36, The Lord will judge His people.

  • v43 — the Greek is much longer: Rejoice, heavens, with Him, and let all the sons of God worship Him. Hebrews 1:6 quotes it, Let all the angels of God worship Him, and Romans 15:10 quotes the line kept in both, Rejoice, nations, with His people.

chapters.title: The Blessing of Moses
chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 33

The LORD Came from Sinai

1This is the blessing with which Moses the man of God blessed the sons of Israel before his death.

2He said:

The LORD came from Sinai
and dawned on them from Seir;
He shone out from Mount Paran
and came from the myriads of holy ones,
from His right hand a fiery law for them.

3Yes, He loves the peoples;
all His holy ones are in Your hand.
They sat down at Your feet;
each receives Your words.

4Moses commanded us an instruction,
a possession for the assembly of Jacob.

5He became king in Jeshurun
when the heads of the people gathered,
the tribes of Israel together.

The Tribes

6Let Reuben live and not die,
though his men be few.

7This is for Judah. He said:
Hear, LORD, the voice of Judah,
and bring him to his people.
With his hands he contends for them;
be a help against his foes.

8Of Levi he said:
Your Thummim and Your Urim belong to Your faithful man,
whom You tested at Massah,
with whom You strove at the waters of Meribah;

9who said of his father and his mother, "I have not seen them,"
and did not acknowledge his brothers,
and did not know his sons.
For they kept Your word
and guarded Your covenant.

10They teach Your rules to Jacob
and Your instruction to Israel;
they put incense before Your face
and whole burnt offerings on Your altar.

11Bless, LORD, his strength,
and accept the work of his hands.
Strike through the loins of those who rise against him,
and of those who hate him, so that they do not rise again.

12Of Benjamin he said:
The beloved of the LORD —
he dwells in safety by Him.
He shields him all the day,
and he dwells between His shoulders.

13Of Joseph he said:
Blessed by the LORD be his land,
with the choicest gifts of heaven, with the dew,
and of the deep that crouches beneath,

14with the choicest fruits of the sun
and the choicest yield of the months,

15with the finest of the ancient mountains
and the choicest of the everlasting hills,

16with the choicest of the earth and its fullness,
and the favor of the One who dwells in the bush.
Let it come on the head of Joseph,
on the crown of the one set apart from his brothers.

17His firstborn bull — majesty is his,
and his horns are the horns of the wild ox.
With them he gores the peoples,
all together, to the ends of the earth.
They are the myriads of Ephraim;
they are the thousands of Manasseh.

18Of Zebulun he said:
Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out,
and Issachar, in your tents.

19They call peoples to the mountain;
there they offer sacrifices of righteousness,
for they suck the abundance of the seas
and the hidden treasures of the sand.

20Of Gad he said:
Blessed is He who enlarges Gad!
He lies down like a lion
and tears the arm, and the crown of the head.

21He chose the first part for himself,
for there the ruler's portion was reserved.
He came with the heads of the people;
he did the righteousness of the LORD
and His judgments with Israel.

22Of Dan he said:
Dan is a lion's cub
that leaps out from Bashan.

23Of Naphtali he said:
Naphtali, satisfied with favor
and full of the blessing of the LORD,
take possession of the sea and the south.

24Of Asher he said:
Most blessed of sons be Asher;
let him be the favored of his brothers,
and let him dip his foot in oil.

25Iron and bronze are your bolts,
and as your days, so your strength.

There Is None Like the God of Jeshurun

26There is none like God, Jeshurun,
who rides the heavens to your help,
and in His majesty the skies.

27The eternal God is a dwelling place,
and underneath are the everlasting arms.
He drove out the enemy before you
and said, "Destroy!"

28So Israel dwells in safety,
the fountain of Jacob alone,
in a land of grain and new wine;
yes, his heavens drip dew.

29Happy are you, Israel! Who is like you,
a people saved by the LORD,
the shield of your help
and the sword of your majesty?
Your enemies will cringe before you,
and you will tread on their high places.

Notes

  • v1 "Moses the man of God" — ish ha-Elohim, the first time the title is used in the Bible. Psalm 90 is headed A prayer of Moses, the man of God.

  • v2 "from Sinai… from Seir… from Mount Paran" — the LORD comes like the sunrise over the southern mountains. A fiery law: the written text has one word, eshdat, and the reading tradition splits it into esh dat, fire, law. What eshdat meant is not known.

  • v3 — difficult Hebrew; the pronouns shift between He and You, as often in these old poems.

  • v8 "Your Thummim and Your Urim" — the order is reversed from Exodus 28:30, the Urim and the Thummim. Levi's place rests on testing at Massah and Meribah.

  • v9 "I have not seen them" — the Levites who rallied to Moses at the calf and did not spare their own (Exodus 32:26–29). Loyalty to God is set above family.

  • v12 "between His shoulders" — Benjamin's land held Jerusalem and the temple; the image may be of God carrying him, or of the sanctuary resting on Benjamin's hills.

  • vv13–16 Joseph — the same words as Jacob's blessing in Genesis 49:26: on the head of Joseph, on the crown of the one set apart from his brothers. The favor of the One who dwells in the bush: seneh, the bush of Exodus 3.

  • v25 "as your days, so your strength" — dove'ekha, a word found nowhere else. Strength is the old guess from context.

  • v26 "There is none like God, Jeshurun" — Jeshurun, the name of 32:15, now in praise. Simeon is the one tribe not named in the blessing.

  • v27 "The eternal God is a dwelling place… underneath are the everlasting arms" — me'onah, dwelling; Psalm 90, A prayer of Moses, the man of God, opens with the same root: Lord, You have been our dwelling place, ma'on. The last word of Moses' blessing about God is that He holds Israel up.

chapters.html:
Deuteronomy 34

Moses Sees the Land

1Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, the top of Pisgah, which is opposite Jericho. The LORD showed him all the land: Gilead as far as Dan,

2all Naphtali, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, all the land of Judah as far as the western sea,

3the Negev, and the plain of the valley of Jericho, the city of palm trees, as far as Zoar.

4The LORD said to him, "This is the land that I swore to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, saying, 'To your seed I will give it.' I have let you see it with your eyes, but you shall not cross over there."

The Death of Moses

5So Moses the servant of the LORD died there in the land of Moab, at the word of the LORD.

6He buried him in the valley in the land of Moab, opposite Beth-peor, and no one knows his burial place to this day.

7Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died. His eye was not dim, and his vigor had not fled.

8The sons of Israel wept for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days, and the days of weeping and mourning for Moses were ended.

9Joshua son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had leaned his hands on him. The sons of Israel listened to him and did as the LORD had commanded Moses.

10There has not risen a prophet since in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face,

11for all the signs and the wonders that the LORD sent him to do in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh and to all his servants and to all his land,

12and for all the mighty hand and all the great terror that Moses did before the eyes of all Israel.

Notes

  • vv1–3 the land from Nebo — the view runs north, then west, then south: Gilead and Dan, Naphtali, Ephraim and Manasseh, Judah to the western sea, the Negev, and down to Zoar. The whole promise is seen, tribe by tribe, before any of it is taken.

  • v4 "To your seed I will give it" — the words of Genesis 12:7, To your seed I will give this land, first spoken to Abram at Shechem. The Torah ends where the promise began.

  • v5 "at the word of the LORD" — al pi YHWH, on the mouth of the LORD, the phrase used of the camp moving and halting at the command of the LORD in the wilderness. Moses the servant dies as he lived, by God's word.

  • v6 "He buried him… no one knows his burial place" — the subject is not named; the natural reading is that God Himself buried Moses. No grave could become a shrine. Jude 9 knows a later story of Michael the archangel disputing about the body of Moses.

  • v7 "His eye was not dim, and his vigor had not fled" — lo nas lecho, his moisture had not fled. In 31:2 he said he could no longer go out and come in; he did not die of age.

  • v8 "thirty days" — the same mourning as for Aaron, Numbers 20:29, all the house of Israel wept for Aaron thirty days.

  • v9 "for Moses had leaned his hands on him" — as commanded in Numbers 27:18, lean your hand on him.

  • vv10–12 "There has not risen a prophet since in Israel like Moses" — the answer, from the far side of his death, to 18:15, a prophet… like me. Face to face: Exodus 33:11, and Numbers 12:8, Mouth to mouth I speak with him. The last words of the Torah are before the eyes of all Israel.
